His words: "The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing."

In His words "Forgiver of sin" there are two possibilities. One is that it means He forgives the sins of the servants; and if this meaning is intended, then the genitive of "forgiver" and "accepter" is on two grounds: one from the intention of repeating "min," so the meaning of the speech then is: "the revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing, from the Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance," because "Forgiver of sin" is indefinite, and it is not most eloquent for an indefinite to be an adjective of a definite; the other is that its i'rāb is made to follow the i'rāb of the first, being indefinite, as an adjective to it, since it falls between it and His words "Possessor of bounty," which is definite. It is also permissible that the i'rāb of the indefinite follow the i'rāb of the first, since it is praise, and praise sometimes follows the i'rāb of what precedes it and sometimes departs from the i'rāb of the first to the accusative or nominative, as the poet said:

"May my people never be far, those who are the poison of enemies and the scourge of the wretched, who descend upon every battle, and the good ones, the knots of the waistwraps."

Ḥadathanā Bishr, who said: Thanā Yazīd, who said: Thanā Saʿīd, from Qatādah, "Ḥā Mīm," he said: a name of the names of the Qur'an.

Others said: it is letters of hijāʾ (spelling/alphabet).

Others said: rather, it is a name, and they argued for their view with the verse of Shurayḥ ibn Awfā al-ʿAbsī:

"It reminds me of Ḥā Mīm while the spear is entangled, so why did he not recite Ḥā Mīm before advancing?"

[The verse is by Shurayḥ ibn Awfā al-ʿAbsī, as Abū ʿUbayd said in Majāz al-Qur'ān (217b) and as in (Lisān al-ʿArab: ḥmm). He said: someone other than Abū ʿUbayd recited it for al-Ashtar al-Nakhaʿī. He said: Ibn Masʿūd said: "Āl Ḥāmīm" is the brocade of the Qur'an. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is like your saying "Āl so-and-so and Āl so-and-so." Al-Jawharī said: as for the common people's saying "al-Ḥawāmīm," it is not from the speech of the Arabs. Abū ʿUbayd said: "al-Ḥawāmīm" are suras in the Qur'an, against analogy, and he recited: "And by the Ṭawāsīn which have been thulith, and by the Ḥawāmīm which have been sabaʿ." He said: the better is to say "those possessing Ḥāmīm." Abū ʿUbayd recited for "Ḥāmīm" the verse of Shurayḥ ibn Awfā al-ʿAbsī: "It reminds me of Ḥāmīm..." He said: someone else recited it for al-Ashtar al-Nakhaʿī. The pronoun in "yudhakkirunī" refers to Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, and he was killed by al-Ashtar or Shurayḥ (i.e., on the day of the Camel). End.]

And al-Kumayt says:

"We found for you in the family of Ḥāmīm a sign, which the pious among us interpreted and the one who expresses it."

[The verse is by al-Kumayt ibn Zayd al-Asadī (Majāz al-Qur'ān of Abū ʿUbaydah 218-1; and his Dīwān, published by al-Mawsūʿāt in Cairo, p. 18). "Āl Ḥāmīm" and "dhawāt Ḥāmīm": the suras beginning with "Ḥā Mīm." Al-Ḥarīrī in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ stated that one says "Āl Ḥāmīm," "dhawāt Ḥāmīm," and "Āl Ṭasm," and one does not say "ḥawāmīm" nor "ṭawāsīm." End. The verse is His saying in Surat al-Shūrā: "Say: I do not ask you any reward for it except affection for the near kin." And in Surat al-Aḥzāb, from the Āl Ḥāmīm: "Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, People of the House, and purify you with thorough purification." Al-Taqī: the one who keeps silent about preference; al-Muʿrib: the one who speaks of it. The narration of the verse in Majāz al-Qur'ān: "We found for you in Ḥā Mīm a sign... and in other than it, verses, and which expresses."]

Thanā... He said: Yūnus said: whoever says this view is rejected by it, because the sura "Ḥā Mīm" has quiescent letters, so it came out in the manner of the letters of spelling, whereas the names of the suras came out vocalized; and if a sura is named after one of these letters (sic), i'rāb enters it. End. The author's words: he means al-Jarmī; we pointed this out earlier, since al-Jarmī's name is Ṣāliḥ ibn Isḥāq Abū ʿUmar.

[Transmitted from Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā that he said: Yūnus, meaning al-Jarmī, said: whoever says this view is rejected by it, because the sura "Ḥā Mīm" has quiescent letters, so it came out in the manner of spelling, and these are names of suras that came out vocalized; and if a sura is named after one of these quiescent letters, i'rāb enters it.]

My view on this is the same as the view on its sisters, which we have explained in His words "Alif Lām Mīm," and that suffices as a reference so as not to repeat it here, since the view on Ḥā Mīm and all that came in the Qur'an in this form—I mean disjointed letters—is one single view.

* *

His words: "The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing."

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: from Allah, the Mighty in His retribution against His enemies, the Knowing of what they do of deeds and other than them, is the revelation of this Book; so "revelation" (tanzīl) is in the nominative by His words "from Allah."

In His words "Forgiver of sin" there are two possibilities. One is that it means He forgives the sins of the servants; and if this meaning is intended, then the genitive of "forgiver" and "accepter" is on two grounds: one from the intention of repeating "min," so the meaning of the speech then is: "the revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing, from the Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance," because "Forgiver of sin" is indefinite, and it is not most eloquent for an indefinite to be an adjective of a definite; the other is that its i'rāb is made to follow the i'rāb of the first, being indefinite, as an adjective to it, since it falls between it and His words "Possessor of bounty," which is definite. It is also permissible that the i'rāb of the indefinite follow the i'rāb of the first, since it is praise, and praise sometimes follows the i'rāb of what precedes it and sometimes departs from the i'rāb of the first to the accusative or nominative, as the poet said:

"May my people never be far, those who are the poison of enemies and the scourge of the wretched, who descend upon every battle, and the good ones, the knots of the waistwraps."

[The two verses are by Khirnaq bint Hifān, from a poem she lamented with regard to her husband Bishr ibn ʿAmr ibn Murthid al-Ḍabʿī and her son ʿAlqamah ibn Bishr and a group of her people who were killed in battle (Khizānat al-Adab al-Kubrā by al-Baghdādī 2:306). The place of testimony in the two verses is that it is permissible to cut the adjective of the definite into nominative by the waw; her saying "wa-l-ṭayyibūn" is an adjective cut to the nominative from "qawmī," for praise and exaltation, making it the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., they are the good ones. And her saying "al-nāzilīn" is cut to the accusative, although it is an adjective of "qawmī" which is genitive. It is accusative by a verb implied, i.e., I praise or I mean, or the like. The author (al-Ṭabarī) cited them as evidence that His words "Forgiver of sin" is an adjective of the word "Allah," genitive by "min"; and in this adjective the genitive is permissible by following, as the accusative is permissible by cutting with an implied verb, i.e., I single out the Forgiver of sin, or the nominative by an implied subject, i.e., He is the Forgiver of sin.]

As He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, Doer of what He intends" (85:14–16), where "Doer" (faʿʿāl) is nominative, and it is a pure indefinite, and it followed the i'rāb of "Forgiving, Loving." The other is that its meaning is that this is part of His attributes, since He has always been forgiving of the sins of the servants, before the descent of this verse, during its descent, and after it; so then it is a correct definite and a correct adjective. He said "Forgiver of sin," not "sins," because the act itself is intended. As for His words "Accepter of repentance," "tawb" may be the plural of "tawbah," as "dawmah" is pluralized as "dawm" and "ʿawmah" (a swimming of a ship) as "ʿawm," as the poet said:

"Swimming of the ships, until what came between them..."

[This is the first half of a verse whose speaker we do not know, nor its second half. The author cited it to show that "tawb" in His words "Accepter of repentance" may be the plural of "tawbah," as "dawmah" is pluralized as "dawm," and "ʿawmah" as "ʿawm," from the swimming of a ship.]

It may also be the verbal noun of "tāba, yatūbu, tawban."

Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Muḥāribī also related to me, who said: Thanā Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: A man came to ʿUmar and said: "I have killed, so is there repentance for me?" He said: "Yes, act and do not despair," then he recited: "Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing, Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance."

* *

His words: "Severe in punishment."

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: severe is His punishment for whoever He punishes of those who disobey Him. So do not rely on the breadth of His mercy, but be wary of Him, by avoiding His acts of disobedience and performing His obligations; for just as He does not despair the people of crime and sin of His pardon and of accepting the repentance of those among them who repent of their wrongdoing, likewise He does not make them safe from His punishment and His retribution against them for what they have made lawful of His sacred things and committed of His acts of disobedience.

* *

His words: "Possessor of bounty."

He says: possessor of grace and blessings spread over whomever He wills of His creation. It is said of someone: "He is a possessor of ṭawl over his companions," when he is possessing favour over them.

The people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ḥadathanī ʿAlī, who said: Thanā Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: Thanī Muʿāwiyah, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words "Possessor of bounty," he said: possessor of abundance and wealth.

Ḥadathanī Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, who said: Thanā Abū ʿĀṣim, who said: Thanā ʿĪsā; and Ḥadathanī al-Ḥārith, who said: Thanā al-Ḥasan, who said: Thanā Warqāʾ, all together, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding the saying of Allah "Possessor of bounty": wealth.

Ḥadathanā Bishr, who said: Thanā Yazīd, who said: Thanā Saʿīd, from Qatādah, "Possessor of bounty": i.e., possessor of blessings.

Some of them said: al-ṭawl means power.

Mention of those who said that:

Ḥadathanā Yūnus, who said: Akhbaranā Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "Possessor of bounty," he said: al-ṭawl is power; that is the ṭawl.

* *

His words: "There is no deity but Him; to Him is the final destination."

He says: there is no worshipped one fit for worship except Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing, whose attributes are what His praise has described; so do not worship anything other than Him. "To Him is the final destination": He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: to Allah is your destination and your return, O people; so worship Him alone, for nothing you have worshipped other than Him will benefit you at that time.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 4–5:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not be deceived by their going back and forth throughout the land. Before them the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them, and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they disputed with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby, so I seized them; then how was My punishment.﴾

His, may He be remembered and exalted, says: None dispute against the proofs of Allah and His evidences for His oneness by denying them, except those who have rejected His monotheism.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So do not be deceived by their going back and forth throughout the land﴾

His, may He be praised and exalted, says: Do not let their movement in the lands, their remaining and their dwelling there, deceive you, O Muhammad, despite their disbelief in their Lord, so that you think they are only being given respite and are free to move about the lands while disbelieving in Allah, and were not hastened with vengeance and punishment for their disbelief because they are upon some truth. Indeed We have not granted them respite for that reason; rather, so that the Book may reach its appointed term, and so that the word of punishment, the punishment of your Lord, may be fulfilled against them.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So do not be deceived by their going back and forth throughout the land﴾: their journeys in it, and their coming and going.

Then He related to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the stories of the nations that denied their messengers, and informed him that in their disputing with their messengers they were upon the like of what his people were upon, to whom he was sent; and that when they reached their term, after the messengers had given them warning and admonished them of His might, He caused His vengeance to descend upon them. He informed His Prophet, through what He mentioned in His Book, that His practice toward his people who followed the path of those in denying and disputing him is the same practice of making His vengeance and might descend upon them. So He, may He be remembered, said: Before your people, who denied your message sent to them as a messenger, the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them who disputed with you in falsehood, namely the nations who banded together and gathered against their messengers in denial of them, such as ʿAd and Thamud, the people of Lot, the companions of Madyan, and their likes.

Those of the interpreters of the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said so:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them﴾: he said, "The disbelievers."

* *

And His saying: ﴿and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾

His, may He be remembered, says: Every nation of these nations that denied their messengers and banded together against their prophets plotted against their messenger who was sent to them, to seize him and then kill him.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾: i.e., to kill him. And it was said "against their messenger" (bi-rasulihim); and it has been said: "every nation," so the pronoun (the hā' and mīm) was directed to the man rather than to the word "nation." It has been mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah it is "bi-rasulihā" (against its messenger), meaning the messenger of the nation.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and they disputed with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby﴾

He says: They contended with their messenger with falsehood of contention, in order to nullify through their disputing with him and their contention against him the truth that came to them from Allah, namely entering into His obedience, affirming His oneness, and disavowing the worship of anything other than Him, just as the disbelievers of your people, O Muhammad, contend with you in falsehood.

* *

And His saying: ﴿so I seized them; then how was My punishment﴾

His, may He be remembered, says: So I seized those who plotted against their messenger to seize him with punishment from Me. So how was My punishment of them? Did I not destroy them, making them a lesson for creation and an admonition for those after them? And did I not make their abodes and dwellings desolate of them, and a resting place for wild beasts?

* And Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿so I seized them; then how was My punishment﴾: he said, "Severe, by Allah."

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as the punishment was decreed against the nations that denied their messengers, whose accounts I have related to you, O Muhammad, and My retribution descended upon them because of their denial of their messengers and their disputing with them falsely, in order that they might thereby refute the truth, so too has the word of your Lord become binding upon those among your people who disbelieved in God, who dispute concerning the signs of God.

* *

As for His words: ﴿that they are the companions of the Fire﴾

The grammarians differed concerning the grammatical position of His words ﴿أنهم (that they)﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: the meaning is: the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire, i.e., because they are, or by virtue of their being. It is not that ﴿أنهم (that they)﴾ is in the position of an object, like your saying: "I have made it true that they..." For if it were so, it would also be "I have made it true, because they..." Others said: ﴿أنهم (that they)﴾ is an apposition (badal) to "the word" (al-kalima), as if he had said: the word was made true, that they are the companions of the Fire.

The correct view on this matter is that His words ﴿أنهم (that they)﴾ are an explanatory rendering (tarjamah) of "the word" (al-kalima), with the meaning: Thus there has been decreed against them the punishment of the Fire, which God promised to the people of disbelief.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 7:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise, and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire."﴾ (7)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who bear the Throne of God among His angels, and those around His Throne, from among the angels who surround it, ﴿glorify their Lord with His praise﴾, meaning they pray to their Lord, praising and thanking Him. ﴿And believe in Him﴾, meaning they affirm before God that there is no god for them besides Him, bear witness to that, and do not disdain to worship Him. ﴿And ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾, meaning they ask their Lord to forgive the sins of those who have affirmed, like their affirmation, the unity of God and the disavowal of every object of worship besides Him, and that He pardon their sins.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾: for the people of "There is no god but God."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge﴾

There is an omitted element in this speech, namely "they say"; the meaning of the speech is: "and ask forgiveness for those who believe, saying: O our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge." By His words ﴿You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ He means: Your mercy and Your knowledge encompass everything of Your creation; You know everything, nothing is hidden from You, and You show mercy to Your creation and encompass them with Your mercy.

The people of Arabic grammar have differed regarding the case of "mercy" and "knowledge." Some grammarians of Basra said: the accusative of these is like the accusative in "laka mithluhu 'abdan" (you have his like as a slave), because you have made "wasi'ta" (You encompassed) govern "kull shay'" (all things), and it is the object of the verb, with the "ta'" as the subject; and "mercy" and "knowledge" came as explanation (tafsir), and you have, with them, occupied the verb as you occupied "mithl" with the pronoun, so you put it in the accusative by analogy with the object after the subject. Another said: it is from what is transferred (manqul), and it is explained: "Your mercy and Your knowledge encompassed," and "He encompassed all things in mercy," just as you say: "my soul was pleased with it" (tabat bihi nafsi), "I was pleased with it in soul" (tibtu bihi nafsan). He said: As for "laka mithluhu 'abdan," the quantities are only known, like "indi ratl zaytan" (I have a pound of oil), and "mithl" is not a known quantity; but its wording is that of a definite noun while "'abd" is indefinite, so "'abd" is put in the accusative, though it may also be in the nominative. He cited for his view the saying of the poet:

"Among Mu'add and all the tribes, nor among Qahtan, is there one counted equal to you"

[[I have not found his source. The author cited it at the verse "Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge," where the people of Arabic differed regarding the accusative of "mercy"... The evidence in the line is "mithlaka wahid" (one equal to you); "wahid" may be taken in apposition to "mithlaka." It may also be an explanation, i.e., a specifier (tamyiz) for "mithl," since although it is definite in wording it is indefinite in meaning, hence it needed explanation (tamyiz), like your saying: "laka mithluhu ardan," "indi faddan ardan," "ratl zaytan," because quantities are only known, and "mithlaka" in meaning is a quantity term. As for the accusative of "mercy" in the verse, the author has explained it.]]

He said: "Wahid" is referred back to "mithl" because it is indefinite. He said: If you said "ma mithluka rajul," "mithluka rajul," or "mithluka rajulan," it would be permissible, because "mithl" is indefinite even though its wording is definite.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾

He says: So pardon the offence of those among Your servants who repent of associating others with You, returning to Your unity, and following Your command and prohibition.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾: from polytheism.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And follow Your way﴾

He says: and they took the path You commanded them to take, and held fast to the method You commanded them to hold to, and that is entering Islam.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And follow Your way﴾: that is, Your obedience.

As for His words: ﴿And protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, He says: Turn away from those who repented of polytheism and followed Your way the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 8:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (8)

He, the Exalted, says, reporting the supplication of His angels for the people of faith among His servants, saying: O ﴿our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden﴾, meaning: gardens of abiding residence, ﴿which You have promised them﴾, meaning: which You promised to those who turn back in obedience to You, that You would admit them into it. ﴿And whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants﴾ means: and admit, along with these who repented and ﴿followed Your way﴾, the Gardens of Eden, those among their fathers, spouses and descendants who were righteous, who acted in the world by what pleases You of righteous deeds. It is mentioned that a man will enter Paradise together with his parents, his children and his wife, even if they did not do his deeds, by the grace of God's mercy toward him.

As it is reported:

Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman al-Ijli narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Sa'id, who said: A man will enter Paradise and say: "Where is my father, where is my mother, where is my child, where is my wife?" It will be said: "They did not do the like of your deeds." He will say: "I used to act for myself and for them." It will be said: "Admit them into Paradise." Then he recited: ﴿Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants.﴾

As for the words "whoever was righteous," being in that sense, they occupy the accusative position as a conjunction (ʿatf) with the pronoun of "them" in His saying ﴿and admit them﴾. It is also permissible that it be in the accusative as a conjunction with the pronoun of "them" in "which You have promised them." ﴿Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ means: Indeed You, O our Lord, are the Exalted in Might in taking vengeance on Your enemies, the Wise in Your management of Your creation.

The commentary on the words of God, exalted is He, in ﴿And protect them from evil deeds. And whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have shown him mercy. That is the great triumph﴾ (40:9)

He, exalted is His remembrance, means by His words, relating the saying of His angels: ﴿And protect them﴾, that is, turn away from them the evil consequence of their misdeeds, which they had committed before their repentance and their turning back to Him. They say: do not hold them accountable for that, so that You punish them for it. ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have shown him mercy﴾ means: and whoever You turn away from the evil consequence of his misdeeds on the Day of Resurrection, You have shown him mercy, and You have delivered him from Your punishment. ﴿And that is the great triumph﴾, because whoever is saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has triumphed, and that is without doubt the great triumph.

Those who practise ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) said in the meaning of "evil deeds" something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾: that is, the punishment.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and from Mutarrif, who said: We found the most sincere of God's servants towards God's servants to be the angels, and the most deceitful of God's servants towards God's servants to be the devils. And he recited ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise﴾... the verse.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Mutarrif said: We found the most deceitful of God's servants towards God's servants to be the devils, and we found the most sincere of God's servants towards God's servants to be the angels.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 10–11:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: The aversion of Allah [toward you] is greater than your aversion toward yourselves, when you were being invited to faith but used to disbelieve.﴾ [40:10] ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice, and we have confessed our sins. So is there any way to get out?"﴾ [40:11]

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Indeed, those who disbelieved in Allah will be called out in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection once they have entered it. They will despise themselves upon entering it, when they witness what Allah has prepared for them within it of various kinds of punishment. It will be said to them: The aversion of Allah toward you, O people, in the worldly life, when you were invited therein to faith in Allah but disbelieved, is greater than your aversion toward yourselves today, because of the wrath of Allah that has descended upon you.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿The aversion of Allah is greater﴾. He said: They despised themselves when they saw their deeds, and Allah's aversion toward them in the world, when they were invited to faith and disbelieved, is greater.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: The aversion of Allah [toward you] is greater than your aversion toward yourselves, when you were being invited to faith but used to disbelieve.﴾ He says: The aversion of Allah toward the people of misguidance, when faith was presented to them in the world and they abandoned it and refused to accept it, is greater than what they despised of themselves when they witnessed the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: The aversion of Allah [toward you] is greater than your aversion toward yourselves﴾ — in the Fire — ﴿when you were being invited to faith﴾ — in the world — ﴿but used to disbelieve﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿They will be called out: The aversion of Allah...﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: When they entered the Fire, they despised themselves for the acts of disobedience to Allah that they had committed, and it was said to them: The aversion of Allah toward you, when He called you to Islam, is more severe than your aversion toward yourselves today, now that you have entered the Fire.

The grammarians differed regarding the reason for this lam appearing in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the aversion of Allah is greater﴾. Some grammarians from Basra said: It is the lam of the beginning (lam al-ibtida'), meaning: "they will be called out, it will be said to them," because calling out involves speech. He said: Similarly in its i'rab, one says: "Lazayd afdalu min Amr" (Zayd is indeed better than Amr). Some grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning is: "they will be called out that the aversion of Allah toward you," but the lam suffices in place of saying in speech: "I called out that Zayd is standing." He said: Similarly His saying: ﴿Then it appeared to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time﴾ [12:35]. The lam has the function of "inna" in every speech that is close to saying, such as "yunadun" (they will be called out) and "yukhbirun" (they will inform), and similar things.

Another grammarian among them said: This is the lam of oath, which enters with a report (hikayah), and what resembles a report, to indicate that what follows it is a fresh beginning (ista'naf). He said: It is not permissible in answers to oaths that it take the place of the oath, because the lam is accompanied by the nun whether or not it is present, so it is sufficient in place of the oath, since it only occurs with it.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: It entered to indicate that what follows it is a fresh beginning, and that it is the lam of oath.

As for His saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾

We have already addressed it in Surah al-Baqarah, which suffices instead of repeating it here, but we will mention some of what others have said about it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. He said: They were dead in the loins of their fathers, then Allah gave them life in the world, then caused them to die the death that is unavoidable, then gave them life for resurrection on the Day of Judgment. So these are two lives and two deaths.

And I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾: it is the saying of Allah: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ [2:28].

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. He said: It is like His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead﴾ ... up to the end of the verse.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, regarding His saying: ﴿You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. He said: It is like that in al-Baqarah: ﴿while you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life﴾.

Abu Husayn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik regarding this verse: ﴿You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. He said: You created us when we were nothing, then You caused us to die, then You gave us life.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying: ﴿You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. They said: They were dead and Allah gave them life, then caused them to die, then gave them life.

Others said regarding this:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. He said: They were made to die in the world, then given life in their graves, so they were questioned or addressed, then they were made to die in their graves, then given life in the Hereafter.

Others said regarding this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice﴾. He said: He created them from the back of Adam when the covenant was taken from them, and he recited: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring﴾ up to ﴿the falsifiers﴾ [7:172–?]. He said: Then He made them forget the act, and took the covenant from them. He said: And He extracted a rib from the lower ribs of Adam and created Hawwa from it, reporting this from the Prophet ﷺ. He said: And that is the saying of Allah: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women﴾ [4:1]. He said: He dispersed from them afterward in the wombs a multitude of creation, and he recited: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾ [39:6]. He said: Creation after that. He said: So when He took the covenant from them, He caused them to die, then created them in the wombs, then caused them to die, then gave them life on the Day of Resurrection. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice, and we have confessed our sins﴾, and he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾ [4:154]. He said: On that day. And he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿Remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [5:7].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 12–14:

The interpretation of the words of God Most High: ﴿That is because, when God alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great.﴾ (12)

In this statement there is an omitted part, which is dispensed with because the apparent meaning indicates it. It is: "So answer that there is no way to that; this is the punishment that is yours, O disbelievers," ﴿because, when God alone was invoked, you disbelieved﴾, so you denied that divinity belongs to Him exclusively, and you said, ﴿Has he made the gods into one god?﴾

﴿But when partners are associated with Him, you believe﴾ means: and if a partner is ascribed to God, you affirm the one who ascribes that to Him. ﴿So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great﴾ means: so the decision belongs to God, the Most High over everything, the Great, before whom everything else is humbled today.

* *

The interpretation of the words of God Most High: ﴿He it is who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky. Yet none is mindful except one who turns back (to God).﴾ (13) ﴿So call upon God, sincere to Him in religion, even though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ (14)

God Most High says: He it is who shows you, O people, His proofs and evidences of His oneness and lordship. ﴿And sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ means: He sends down for you your sustenance from the sky by pouring abundant rain, by which He brings forth your food from the earth and the fodder of your livestock, as a favour to you. ﴿Yet none is mindful except one who turns back﴾ means: none takes heed of the proofs of God which He made as evidence of His oneness, so that he is admonished by them and learns the reality of what they indicate, except one who turns back, that is, who returns to His monotheism and turns to His obedience.

As:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿except one who turns back﴾: he said, "One who turns to the obedience of God."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾

God Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and to the believers in him: worship God, O believers, sincere to Him in obedience, without associating with Him anything else besides Him, ﴿even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ means: even if the disbelievers, who associate idols and rivals in their worship, dislike your worshipping Him sincerely in obedience.

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿except one who turns back﴾: he said, "One who turns to the obedience of God."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾

God Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and to the believers in him: worship God, O believers, sincere to Him in obedience, without associating with Him anything else besides Him, ﴿even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ means: even if the disbelievers, who associate idols and rivals in their worship, dislike your worshipping Him sincerely in obedience.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne. He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants, that He may warn of the Day of Mutual Meeting (15). The Day when they will come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. "Whose is the dominion today?" "It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer" (16).﴾

His Exalted Remembrance says: He is Exalted in degrees. The raising of His words ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾ is by way of beginning (a new sentence, mubtada'); had it come in the accusative as a response to His words "so call upon Allah," it would have been correct. ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ means: Possessor of the throne that encompasses what is below it.

And His words: ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾

That is: He sends down revelation by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants.

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the meaning of "the Spirit" (al-ruh) in this place. Some of them said: it refers to revelation (al-wahy).

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command﴾: "the revelation from His command."

Others said: it refers to the Qur'an and the Book.

Those who said this:

* Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mihrabi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾: he said: by "the Spirit" is meant the Book which He sends down upon whomever He wills.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾, and he recited: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit from Our command﴾, and said: this Qur'an is the Spirit, which Allah revealed to Jibril, and Jibril is a Spirit who descended with it upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has descended with it﴾. He said: So the books which Allah sent down to His prophets are the Spirit, "that he may warn of the Day of Meeting" (in which) ﴿the Spirit and the angels will stand in ranks﴾. He said: The Spirit is the Qur'an; my father used to say this. Ibn Zayd said: They will stand in ranks for Him between heaven and earth when His majesty descends.

Others said: it refers to prophethood.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾: he said: prophethood upon whomever He wills.

These sayings are close in meaning, even though their wordings differ.

And His words: ﴿that He may warn of the Day of Meeting﴾

That is: He casts it upon whomever of His servants He wills, that he may warn, from among His creation, of the punishment of a day on which the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet, and that is the Day of Meeting (al-talaq), which is the Day of Resurrection.

The people of interpretation have spoken in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah magnified and warned His servants against.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾: the day on which the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet, and the Creator and the creation.

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾, the meeting of the people of the heavens and the people of the earth.

* Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾: he said: the Day of Resurrection, the day when the servants meet one another.

And His words: ﴿The Day when they will come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah﴾

By His words ﴿The Day when they will come forth﴾ He means those who were warned, to whom Allah sent His messengers to warn them, and they are manifest, meaning visible to observers, with no mountain or tree coming between them and seeing them, and no screen concealing some of them from others; rather they will be on a level plain, with no crookedness or elevation in it. The "they" (hum) in His words ﴿yawmihim﴾ is in a place of raising by what follows it, as in the speaker's saying: "I did that on the day of al-Hajjaj, the governor."

The grammarians of Arabic differed over the reason why "hum" was not put in the genitive after "yawm," though "yawm" is annexed to it. Some grammarians of Basra said: "yawm" is annexed to "hum" in meaning, and therefore "al-yawm" is not given tanwin, as in His words ﴿The day when they will be tried over the Fire﴾ and His words ﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾; its meaning is: this is the day of their trial. But when the noun was begun and built upon, it could not be put in the genitive, and the annexation in meaning was to the trial. This happens only when the day has the sense of "idh" (when); otherwise it is ugly. Do you not see that you say: "I wish you were in the time of Zayd as governor," meaning "when Zayd is governor"? If you said: "I will meet you in the time of Zayd is governor," it would not be good. Another said: the meaning of that is that times have been made to carry the sense of "idh" and "idha," therefore they remain in their accusative form in the nominative, genitive and accusative, as He said: ﴿and from the disgrace of that day﴾, where they used the accusative while the place is genitive. This is evidence that it was made to occupy the place of the particle. It may also be inflected with the full range of inflections, since it has become manifest like nouns; do you not see that a pronoun does not refer back to it as it refers back to nouns? If a pronoun does refer back to it, it takes tanwin and is inflected and not annexed, so one says: "The day in which you say pleased me," since it has left the sense of a particle and a reference to it has come back, and it has become a sound noun. He said: It is permissible with "idh" that you say: "I came to you when (idh) you stand," just as you say: "I came to you on the day the judge sits," where it is a known time. As for "I came to you on the day you stand," there is no difficulty in it, and it is permissible according to all of them. He said: this is what is called a non-pure (ghayr mahda) annexation.

The correct view in my opinion regarding this is that the accusative of "yawm" and the other times in such a position is like the accusative of particles, because they occupy their positions; and when they are inflected with the full range of inflections, that is because they have become manifest like nouns, and so they are treated as such.

And His words: ﴿nothing of them being hidden from Allah﴾

That is: nor of their deeds which they did in the world, ﴿nothing﴾.

Qatada used to say about this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿The Day when they will come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah﴾: but they will come forth before Him on the Day of Resurrection, so they will not be concealed by a rope or a clod.

And His words: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾

That is: the Lord says: whose is the dominion today? The phrase "He says" is omitted, being understood from the context.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ (40:17)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, relating His words on the Day of Resurrection, when He raises His creation from their graves to the place of reckoning: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾. He means: today every doer will be rewarded for his deed, and his wage for his work will be paid in full. So the doer of good is repaid with good, and the doer of evil is repaid with its recompense.

* *

And His saying: ﴿There is no injustice today﴾.

He means: no diminishing will be done to anyone regarding the reward for his deed in this world that he has earned, so that it is reduced for him if he was a doer of good, nor will the burden of a sin that he did not commit be laid upon an evildoer so that he is punished for it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. He means: indeed Allah is swift in calling His servants to account that Day for the deeds they did in this world. It has been mentioned that this day will not be half over before the people of Paradise take their rest in Paradise and the people of the Fire take their rest in the Fire, having finished their reckoning and the judgment between them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 18–20:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief. The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed. (18) He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. (19) And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him judge nothing. Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ (20)

His Exalted mention says to His Prophet: Warn, O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people of the Imminent Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, that they will meet Allah on it with their vile deeds, and so deserve His painful punishment.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿the Imminent Day﴾, he said: the Day of Resurrection.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day﴾, he said: the Day of Resurrection.

* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day﴾, he said: the Day of Resurrection, and he recited: ﴿The Imminent One has drawn near; none besides Allah can remove it.﴾

And His saying: ﴿when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief﴾

His Exalted mention says: When the hearts of the servants, out of fear of Allah's punishment, will be at their throats, having risen from their breasts and lodged in their gullets, choking with grief, wishing to return them to their places in their breasts but they will not return, nor will they leave their bodies so that they die.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿when hearts are at the throats﴾, he said: the hearts will have reached the throats from dread, so they neither come out nor return to their places.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿when hearts are at the throats, choking with grief﴾, he said: their hearts will have risen from their places, lodged in their throats, so they do not come out from their bellies and die, nor return to their places and settle.

The grammarians differed regarding the accusative case of ﴿kazimin (choking with grief)﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), as if he meant: when the hearts are at the throats in this state. Some grammarians of Kufa used to say: the alif and lam (in al-qulub and al-hanajir) are substitutes for the possessive pronoun, as if he said: when their hearts are at their throats in the state of their choking. Another of them said: it is an accusative of qat' (a shift to a separate description) from the meaning that returns from their mention in "the hearts" and "the throats," the implied sense being: when their hearts are at their throats, choking. He said: if you wish, you may take it as a detached part of the pronoun in His saying ﴿and warn them﴾. He said: the first is better in Arabic, and the explanation of this has already been given.

His saying: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor﴾

His Exalted mention says: The disbelievers in Allah will have on that day no intimate friend who cares (yahummu) for them, who would repel from them the great calamity that has befallen them of Allah's punishment, nor any intercessor who will intercede for them with their Lord and be obeyed in what he intercedes for, and whose request is granted.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor﴾, he said: one who is concerned with their affair; and they will have no intercessor.

His saying: ﴿yuta' (who will be obeyed)﴾

It is a relative clause qualifying "intercessor." The meaning of the speech: The wrongdoers have no intimate friend, nor an intercessor who, if he interceded, would be obeyed in what he interceded for, and his intercession would be accepted for them.

His saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾

His Exalted mention, describing His own attribute, says: Your Lord knows what the eyes of His servants betray, and what their breasts conceal, meaning what their hearts harbour; that is, nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, even what a person speaks to himself and what his heart harbours when he looks, regarding what he intends by his glance and what he resolves in his heart. ﴿And Allah judges with truth﴾: that is, Allah, the Exalted, judges, concerning what the eyes betray by their glance and what the breasts conceal at the sight of the eyes, with truth, so He will recompense those who lower their gaze and turn their sight away from His prohibitions, out of fear of standing before Him and being questioned about it, with the best reward, and those who let their glance wander and whose hearts resolve to commit abominations when they have the power, with their due recompense.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Husayn ibn Waqid told us, saying: my father told me, saying: al-A'mash told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr told us, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾: when you look at them desiring treachery or not; ﴿and what the breasts conceal﴾: when you have power over them, whether you commit fornication with them or not. He said: then he fell silent, then said: Shall I inform you of what follows it? I said: Yes. He said: ﴿And Allah judges with truth﴾: He is able to recompense good with good and evil with evil. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ Al-Hasan said: I said to al-A'mash: al-Kalbi narrated to me, except that he said: Indeed Allah is able to recompense evil with evil and good with tenfold. Al-A'mash said: What is with al-Kalbi is with me; it has come out of me only in a corrupted form.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾: he said: the glances of the eyes toward what Allah has forbidden.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿the treachery of the eyes﴾: that is, He knows the furtive glance of the eye and the lowering of the gaze toward what Allah does not love or approve.

His saying: ﴿And those they invoke besides Him judge nothing﴾

He says: The idols and deities which these polytheists of your people worship besides Allah judge nothing, because they know nothing and have no power over anything. His Exalted mention says to them: Worship Him who is able over everything, nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, so that He recompenses the good-doer among you with good and the evil-doer with evil; not what has no power over anything and knows nothing, so that it would distinguish the good-doer from the evil-doer, rewarding the one and punishing the other.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾

He says: Indeed Allah is the Hearing of what your tongues utter, O people, and the Seeing of the deeds you do; He encompasses all of that and records it against you, so that He may recompense all of you with your recompense on the Day of Recompense.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it: "وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ" with the letter ta' (addressing the audience). The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the letter ya' (as a third-person report).

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known readings, sound in meaning, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day﴾, he said: the Day of Resurrection.

* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day﴾, he said: the Day of Resurrection, and he recited: ﴿The Imminent One has drawn near; none besides Allah can remove it.﴾

And His saying: ﴿when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief﴾

His Exalted mention says: When the hearts of the servants, out of fear of Allah's punishment, will be at their throats, having risen from their breasts and lodged in their gullets, choking with grief, wishing to return them to their places in their breasts but they will not return, nor will they leave their bodies so that they die.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿when hearts are at the throats﴾, he said: the hearts will have reached the throats from dread, so they neither come out nor return to their places.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿when hearts are at the throats, choking with grief﴾, he said: their hearts will have risen from their places, lodged in their throats, so they do not come out from their bellies and die, nor return to their places and settle.

The grammarians differed regarding the accusative case of ﴿kazimin (choking with grief)﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), as if he meant: when the hearts are at the throats in this state. Some grammarians of Kufa used to say: the alif and lam (in al-qulub and al-hanajir) are substitutes for the possessive pronoun, as if he said: when their hearts are at their throats in the state of their choking. Another of them said: it is an accusative of qat' (a shift to a separate description) from the meaning that returns from their mention in "the hearts" and "the throats," the implied sense being: when their hearts are at their throats, choking. He said: if you wish, you may take it as a detached part of the pronoun in His saying ﴿and warn them﴾. He said: the first is better in Arabic, and the explanation of this has already been given.

His saying: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor﴾

His Exalted mention says: The disbelievers in Allah will have on that day no intimate friend who cares (yahummu) for them, who would repel from them the great calamity that has befallen them of Allah's punishment, nor any intercessor who will intercede for them with their Lord and be obeyed in what he intercedes for, and whose request is granted.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor﴾, he said: one who is concerned with their affair; and they will have no intercessor.

His saying: ﴿yuta' (who will be obeyed)﴾

It is a relative clause qualifying "intercessor." The meaning of the speech: The wrongdoers have no intimate friend, nor an intercessor who, if he interceded, would be obeyed in what he interceded for, and his intercession would be accepted for them.

His saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾

His Exalted mention, describing His own attribute, says: Your Lord knows what the eyes of His servants betray, and what their breasts conceal, meaning what their hearts harbour; that is, nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, even what a person speaks to himself and what his heart harbours when he looks, regarding what he intends by his glance and what he resolves in his heart. ﴿And Allah judges with truth﴾: that is, Allah, the Exalted, judges, concerning what the eyes betray by their glance and what the breasts conceal at the sight of the eyes, with truth, so He will recompense those who lower their gaze and turn their sight away from His prohibitions, out of fear of standing before Him and being questioned about it, with the best reward, and those who let their glance wander and whose hearts resolve to commit abominations when they have the power, with their due recompense.

The people of interpretation said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Husayn ibn Waqid told us, saying: my father told me, saying: al-A'mash told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr told us, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾: when you look at them desiring treachery or not; ﴿and what the breasts conceal﴾: when you have power over them, whether you commit fornication with them or not. He said: then he fell silent, then said: Shall I inform you of what follows it? I said: Yes. He said: ﴿And Allah judges with truth﴾: He is able to recompense good with good and evil with evil. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ Al-Hasan said: I said to al-A'mash: al-Kalbi narrated to me, except that he said: Indeed Allah is able to recompense evil with evil and good with tenfold. Al-A'mash said: What is with al-Kalbi is with me; it has come out of me only in a corrupted form.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾: he said: the glances of the eyes toward what Allah has forbidden.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿the treachery of the eyes﴾: that is, He knows the furtive glance of the eye and the lowering of the gaze toward what Allah does not love or approve.

His saying: ﴿And those they invoke besides Him judge nothing﴾

He says: The idols and deities which these polytheists of your people worship besides Allah judge nothing, because they know nothing and have no power over anything. His Exalted mention says to them: Worship Him who is able over everything, nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, so that He recompenses the good-doer among you with good and the evil-doer with evil; not what has no power over anything and knows nothing, so that it would distinguish the good-doer from the evil-doer, rewarding the one and punishing the other.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾

He says: Indeed Allah is the Hearing of what your tongues utter, O people, and the Seeing of the deeds you do; He encompasses all of that and records it against you, so that He may recompense all of you with your recompense on the Day of Recompense.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it: "وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ" with the letter ta' (addressing the audience). The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known readings, sound in meaning, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 21–22:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.﴾ (21)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Have these people who persist in their polytheism toward Allah, who deny His Messenger from among the Quraysh, not travelled through the lands, ﴿and seen what was the end of those who were before them﴾ — meaning: that they may see what became the final outcome of the nations who were before them, the nations who followed their path in disbelief in Allah and denial of His messengers. ﴿They were greater than them in strength⦆ — meaning: those nations who were before them were mightier than them in might and more lasting upon the earth in traces, and the strength of their powers and the greatness of their bodies did not benefit them when the command of Allah came to them and seized them for what they had committed of His disobedience and the sins they had earned. Rather, He destroyed their multitude, and their dwellings became desolate of them because of what they had wronged. ﴿And they had no protector against Allah﴾ — meaning: they had no one to shield them from the punishment of Allah when it came to them, who would ward it off and repel it from them.

As related by:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and they had no protector against Allah﴾: who would shield them, and it would not benefit them.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾ (22)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: This which We did to those nations who were before the polytheists of Quraysh, of destroying them for their sins, We did to them because their messengers, sent by Allah to them, came with clear proofs — meaning, with the signs that demonstrate the truth of what they called them to: the Oneness of Allah and submission to His obedience. ﴿But they disbelieved⦆ — meaning: they denied their messengership, rejected the Oneness of Allah, and refused to obey Allah. ﴿So Allah seized them⦆ — meaning: Allah seized them with His punishment and destroyed them. ﴿Indeed, He is Strong, Severe in punishment⦆ — meaning: Allah is possessed of power that nothing can overcome, nothing subdues Him, and nothing can frustrate what He wills; His punishment is severe upon whomever of His creatures He punishes. This is a warning from Allah to the polytheists of Quraysh who deny His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: Beware, O people, lest you follow their path in denying Muhammad (ﷺ), rejecting the Oneness of Allah, and opposing His command and prohibition, for then He will make you travel their path toward swift destruction.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 25–26:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women." But the plotting of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.﴾ (25)

He, the Exalted, says: So when Moses came to these people, to whom Allah sent him, with the truth from Us, that is, his coming to them with the Oneness of Allah and acting in obedience to Him, together with establishing the proof against them, that Allah had sent him to them to call them to that, ﴿they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe"﴾ in Allah ﴿with him﴾ from the Children of Israel, ﴿and spare their women﴾. He says: spare their women and keep them alive for service.

If someone says: How is it said, ﴿So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women,"﴾ when the killing of the boys of the Children of Israel by Pharaoh was out of fear of the child who had been foretold would be the cause of the ruin of his kingdom and the destruction of his people, and that was, as is said, before Allah sent Moses as a prophet? It is said: This command to kill the sons of those who believed with Moses and to spare their women was a command from Pharaoh and his chiefs after the first command which Pharaoh had issued before Moses' birth.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women."﴾ He said: This is a killing other than the first killing that had taken place.

* *

And His saying: ﴿But the plotting of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.﴾

He says: the scheming of the people of disbelief against the people of faith in Allah is nothing but in deviation from the path of truth, turning away from the straight course, and taking a way without guidance.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 40, verses 27–28**

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "Leave me, let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land."﴾ (26)

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾ to his chiefs (al-mala'): ﴿"Leave me, let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord"﴾, meaning the one he claims has sent him to us, so that his Lord may protect him from us. ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾ means: I fear that he will alter your religion, which you follow, through his sorcery.

The reciters (al-qurra') differed over the recitation of His words: ﴿or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madinah, Syria and Basra recited it as "wa-an yuzhira fi al-ardi al-fasad" (and that he will cause corruption to appear in the land), without an alif (أَنْ without أَوْ), and this is how it appears in the codices of the people of Madinah. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as ﴿aw an﴾ (أَوْ أَنْ) with an alif, and this is how it appears in their codices, as "yaẓhara fi al-ardi" with a fatha on the yā' and the fasād in the nominative (raf').

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that both are well-known recitations among the regional reciters, and their meanings are close. This is because when someone causes corruption to appear, it becomes apparent, and when it appears, it appears through the one who causes it to appear. So, the recitation of either of the two readings clearly indicates the correctness of the meaning of the other. As for the recitation of ﴿an yuzhira﴾ with the alif and without it, their meanings are also close, because when a thing is changed into its opposite, there is no doubt that its opposite, into which it was first changed, is the apparent one and not the changed one. Therefore, whether it is coordinated with his statement about his fear of Moses, that he will change their religion, using the particle wa (وَ, "and") or aw (أَوْ, "or"), it makes no difference, because for him the changing of their religion was the appearing of corruption, and the appearing of corruption was, for him, the changing of religion.

So the meaning of the statement is: Indeed, I fear from Moses that he will change your religion which you follow, or that he will make appear in your land, the land of Egypt, the worship of his Lord, to whom he calls you to worship; and that, in his view, was corruption.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾: that is, your affair which you follow. ﴿Or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾: and corruption, in his view, is that they obey Allah.

* * *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning." (27) And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said: "Would you kill a man for saying, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, upon him is his lie; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar."﴾ (28)

He, the Exalted, says: Moses said to Pharaoh and his chiefs: "Indeed, I have sought protection, O people, in my Lord and your Lord, from every arrogant one who is proud against His oneness, and against acknowledging His divinity and obeying Him, who does not believe in the Day on which Allah will reckon His creatures, and recompense the good-doer for his good and the wrongdoer for what he has done." Moses, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, specifically sought refuge in Allah from the one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning, because one who does not affirm the Day of Reckoning does not hope for reward for good deeds, nor fear punishment for evil deeds, and does not fear the ugliness of the actions he commits. For this reason, his seeking refuge was specifically from this category of people.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said﴾

The scholars differed regarding this believing man. Some of them said: He was from Pharaoh's people, except that he had believed in Moses, and he used to hide his faith from Pharaoh and his people, fearing for his own life.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh﴾: he said: He was the cousin of Pharaoh.

It is also said that he is the one who was saved along with Moses. Whoever holds this view and interprets it this way, then it is correct to pause (waqf) if the reader wishes to stop at His words ﴿from the family of Pharaoh﴾, because that is a complete statement that has concluded.

Others said: Rather, the man was an Israelite, but he concealed his faith from the family of Pharaoh.

According to this view, the correct pause for one who wishes to stop is at His words ﴿who concealed his faith﴾, because His words ﴿from the family of Pharaoh﴾ are a complement (silah) to His words ﴿who concealed his faith﴾, so its completion is His words "who concealed his faith." It has been mentioned that the name of this believing man from the family of Pharaoh was Jibril (Gabriel). Thus Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq.

The most correct of the two views in my opinion is the view stated by al-Suddi: that the believing man was from the family of Pharaoh, who listened to his words, and heard from him what he said, and refrained from killing Moses when he forbade killing him. And he said what he said, and he said to them: "I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct." And if he had been an Israelite, it would have been likely that this killer of his, and his chiefs, would have hastened to punish him for his statement, because they did not seek counsel from the Children of Israel, considering them enemies to him. So how could his words about killing Moses be (acceptable) if he found a way to it? Rather, since he was one of the chiefs of his people, they listened to his words and withheld from what they had intended regarding Moses.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Would you kill a man for saying, "My Lord is Allah"﴾

He says: "Would you, O people, kill Moses for saying, 'My Lord is Allah'?" The phrase ﴿an yaqula﴾ (أَنْ يَقُولَ, "for saying") is in the accusative position (nasb) as I have described. ﴿And he has come to you with clear proofs﴾ means: he has come to you with clear signs proving the truth of what he says about that. And those clear proofs from the signs were his hand and his staff.

As follows:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿and he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾: with his staff and his hand.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And if he is a liar, upon him is his lie﴾

He says: And if Moses is a liar in his claim that Allah has sent him to you, commanding you to worship Him and to abandon your religion which you follow, then the sin of his lie is upon him alone, not upon you. ﴿But if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you﴾ means: and if he is truthful in what he says, there will befall you some of the punishment he has promised you for remaining upon the religion you hold, so you have no need to kill him, lest you increase your Lord's wrath against you by your disbelief. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾ means: Indeed, Allah does not grant success to the truth to one who oversteps by doing what is not his to do, and who lies against Allah, saying falsehood and what is not true about Him.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of "transgressor" (musrif) which the believer mentioned in this place. Some of them said: It refers to polytheism, meaning: Indeed, Allah does not guide one who associates partners with Him and fabricates against Him.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾: a polytheist who has transgressed against himself through polytheism.

Others said: It refers to one who is a habitual killer, a shedder of blood without right.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾: he said: The transgressor is the one with blood (on his hands). It is also said: They are the polytheists.

The correct view on this is to say: Allah informed about this believer that he spoke in general terms with His words ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾. Polytheism is a form of transgression (israf), and shedding blood without right is a form of transgression, and both of these were gathered in Pharaoh. Therefore, the truth is that this is to be understood generally, just as He, the Majestic and Praised, informed about the one who spoke these words, that he spoke them in general terms.
