He means the people of Abraham and the people of Lot, and they too were among the factions (al-Ahzab).

As follows:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And those after them﴾: he said, "They are the factions."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice to the servants﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning the statement of the believer from the family of Pharaoh to Pharaoh and his chiefs: Allah did not destroy these factions among these nations as an injustice from Him toward them, without any crime they had committed between them and Him, for He does not desire the injustice of His servants, nor does He will it. Rather, He destroyed them for their crimes, their disbelief in Him, and their opposition to His command.

The exegesis of the words of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out (al-tanad)﴾ [40:32] ... wait, let me translate precisely the given text.

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Mutual Calling (yawm al-tanad)* (32) The Day you turn back fleeing; you will have no protector from Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide (33)﴾**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, reporting the words of this believer to Pharaoh and his people: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you﴾ — for killing Moses, if you kill him — the punishment of Allah ﴿the Day of Mutual Calling﴾.

The reciters differed in reading His saying: ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read it ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾ with the *dal* lightened (takhfif) and the *ya'* omitted, in the sense of *tafa'ul* (reciprocal form), from *tanadda al-qawm tanadiyan* (the people called out to one another), as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, "We have found true what our Lord promised us, so have you found true what your Lord promised?" They will say, "Yes"﴾ [7:44]. And He said: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water..."﴾ [7:50]. Therefore, those who read it this way interpreted it accordingly.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that he said regarding this verse, ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾: "The day when the people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise: 'Pour upon us some water.'"

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Mutual Calling﴾: "The day when the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire, ﴿that we have found true what our Lord promised us, so have you found true what your Lord promised?﴾ and the people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise, ﴿'Pour upon us some water or of what Allah has provided you'﴾."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾: "On the Day of Resurrection the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire."

It has been reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, regarding the meaning of this reading, another interpretation different from this one:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah commands Israfil with the First Blast, and He says: 'Blow the blast of terror.' So the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth are terrified, except whom Allah wills. Allah commands him to prolong it and sustain it, and it does not cease. It is the one of which Allah says: ﴿And they await but a single blast, with no respite﴾ [38:15]. Then Allah sets the mountains in motion, and they become a mirage, and the earth shakes with its people in a violent shaking. It is the one of which Allah says: ﴿On the Day the quaker quakes, followed by the follower; hearts that Day will be trembling﴾ [79:6–8]. It becomes like a ship tossed in the sea, struck by the waves, lurching with its people, or like a lamp hung from the Throne, shaken by the winds. People sway upon its back; nursing mothers forget, pregnant women miscarry, children turn gray, and the devils fly away fleeing until they reach the horizons, where the angels meet them and strike their faces, so they turn back. People turn away fleeing, calling out to one another. It is this of which Allah says: ﴿The Day of Mutual Calling, the Day you turn back fleeing; you will have no protector from Allah﴾."

According to this interpretation, the meaning of the speech is: "And O my people, indeed I fear for you the day when people call out to one another from the terror of the Blast of Terror."

Others read it: "yawm al-tannad" with the *dal* doubled (tashdid), in the sense of the reciprocal form from *al-nadd* (fleeing), which is when they flee and scatter across the earth, as camels bolt when they run off from their herders.

Mention of those who said this, and mention of the meaning intended by reading it so:

Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah commands the lowest heaven, and it splits open with its inhabitants, and those in it of the angels descend and surround the earth and those upon it. Then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they line up row behind row. Then the Supreme King descends upon its left side, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they flee, and they do not reach any region of the earth without finding seven rows of angels, so they return to the place where they were. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed I fear for you the Day of Mutual Calling, the Day you turn back fleeing﴾. And that is His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank, and Hell is brought forward that Day﴾ [89:22–23], and His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [55:33], and that is His saying: ﴿And the heaven will split open, for it that Day is frail, and the angels will be upon its edges﴾ [69:16–17]."

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾: "You will flee (tanidduna)."

It has been related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he read it: "yawm al-tanadi," with the *ya'* affirmed and the *dal* lightened.

The correct reading in our view is what the reciters of the major cities agree upon: the *dal* lightened and without the *ya'*, because this is the reading upon which the proof is agreed by the reciters of the major cities, and it is not permissible to oppose it in what has come down by transmission. If this is the correct reading, then the meaning of the speech is: "And O my people, indeed I fear for you the day when people call out to one another, either from the awe of what they have witnessed of the great authority of Allah and the horror of the distress that overtakes them on that day, or for some of them to remind others of Allah's fulfillment of the promise He made to them in the world, and for some to seek help from others against the great affliction they suffer therein."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The Day you turn back fleeing﴾

Its interpretation, according to the interpretation we mentioned from the report of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "The day they turn back fleeing across the earth, fearing the punishment and retribution of Allah, when they see Hell face to face."

Its interpretation according to the interpretation said by Qatadah regarding the meaning of ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾: the day you turn back departing from the place of reckoning toward Hell.

A report similar to this has been transmitted from him, and from those who said similarly regarding the meaning of ﴿yawm al-tanad﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿The Day you turn back fleeing﴾: "That is, going off with you to the Fire."

The more correct of the two views is the one transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, although what Qatadah said is not far from the truth, and a group of the people of interpretation said it.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿The Day you turn back fleeing﴾: "Fleeing, not escaping."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾

It means: you will have no preventer from Allah who will prevent you, nor helper who will help you.

The people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾: "That is, no helper."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾

It means: whoever Allah forsakes and does not grant success to his rightful guidance, he has no one to grant him success in it.

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Joseph certainly brought you clear proofs before, but you remained in doubt about what he had brought you, until, when he died, you said, "Allah will never send after him a messenger." Thus does Allah leave astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter﴾ [40:34].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And Joseph, the son of Jacob, certainly brought you, O my people, clear proofs before Moses, from among the evident proofs of Allah."

As related:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And Joseph certainly brought you clear proofs before﴾, he said: "Before Moses."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿but you remained in doubt about what he had brought you﴾:

He says: "You continued to be doubtful about what Joseph brought you from your Lord, your hearts not being certain of its truth. ﴿Until, when he died﴾" means: until, when Joseph died, you, O people, said: "Allah will not send to you after Joseph any messenger calling to the truth." ﴿Thus does Allah leave astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter﴾" means: Thus does Allah turn away from reaching the truth and from the right path whoever is a disbeliever in it and a doubter, one who is in doubt concerning the reality of the reports of His messengers.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 35:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them. It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal every heart of an arrogant tyrant.﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, relating the statement of the believing man from the people of Pharaoh: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them﴾. So His words "those who" are a reference back to "whoever" in His words ﴿whoever is a transgressor, a doubter﴾. The meaning of the speech is: Thus does Allah lead astray the people of excess and extremism in their misguidance, through their disbelief in Allah, their audacity toward His disobedience, and their doubt concerning the reports of His messengers, those who dispute about His proofs which His messengers brought to them, seeking to refute them with falsehood among the proofs. ﴿Without authority having come to them﴾ means: without a proof having come to them from their Lord by which they could repel the reality of the proofs which the messengers brought to them. And "those who," when the meaning of the speech is as we have mentioned, is in the accusative position as a reference back to "whoever."

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah﴾

It means: that dispute with which they dispute concerning the signs of Allah is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah, ﴿and in the sight of those who believe﴾ in Allah. The word ﴿hateful﴾ is in the accusative because of the pronoun of the dispute implied in His words ﴿greatly﴾. It is similar to His words: ﴿A word that comes out of their mouths is greatly [monstrous]﴾. Whoever puts "word" in the accusative does so because he takes the pronoun of their saying, ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾, to be implied in the verb "greatly." As for whoever does not imply that, he puts "word" in the nominative.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus does Allah seal every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾

It means: just as Allah sealed the hearts of the transgressors who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them, so Allah seals every heart that is arrogant toward Allah, refusing to affirm His oneness and to believe His messengers. "Tyrant" means: one who exalts himself against following the truth.

The reciters differed concerning the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the regional centers recited it, except Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, as: ﴿every heart of an arrogant﴾, with the heart attributed to the arrogant, meaning a report that Allah sealed the hearts of all the arrogant. For whoever has this reading, "tyrant" is a description of "arrogant." It has been related from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite it: "Thus does Allah seal the heart of every arrogant tyrant."

It was narrated to me by Ibn Yusuf, who said: al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Harun, that it was thus in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. This which is reported from Ibn Mas'ud's reading confirms the reading of those who read it with the heart attributed to the arrogant, because placing "every" before "heart" or after it does not change the meaning; rather the meaning is one in both cases. It has been reported from some Arabs by transmission: "He combs his hair every Friday," meaning every Friday day. As for Abu Amr, he read it with the heart nunated and without attributing it to "arrogant," making "arrogant" and "tyrant" descriptions of the heart.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who read it with the heart attributed to the arrogant, because arrogance is the act of the doer with his heart, just as the killer, when he kills a victim, even if he killed with his hand, the act is attributed to him; the heart is a limb of the arrogant, and though arrogance resides in it, the act is ascribed to its doer. This is similar to what we have said about killing. And although that is as we have said, the other reading is not rejected, because the Arabs do not forbid saying "the hand of so-and-so struck," "his eyes saw such-and-such," and "his heart understood," attributing the actions to the limbs, even though in reality they belong to their owners.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 36–37:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways (al-asbab)—the ways of the heavens—and look upon the God of Moses, though I think he is a liar." And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the way. And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Pharaoh said, when the believer from his family admonished him with what he admonished him and warned him against killing Moses, the prophet of Allah, and cautioned him of the might of Allah for his saying "I will kill him," to his vizier, the evil vizier Haman: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the asbab,﴾ meaning: a building.

We have already explained the meaning of al-sarh (tower) earlier, with its evidences, in a manner that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

﴿That I may reach the asbab﴾: the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-asbab in this place. Some of them said: "The asbab of the heavens" means their paths.

Those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Israel, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿asbab al-samawat﴾ he said: the paths of the heavens.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿I may reach the asbab, the asbab of the heavens﴾ he said: the paths of the heavens.

Others said: What is meant by the asbab of the heavens is the gates of the heavens.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build for me a tower"﴾ — and he was the first to build with this baked brick and fire it — ﴿that I may reach the asbab, the asbab of the heavens﴾: i.e., the gates of the heavens.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is the abode of the heaven.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: ﴿that I may reach the asbab, the asbab of the heavens﴾: he said: the abode of the heaven.

We have already explained earlier that the sabab is everything by which one makes a means to reach what is sought, such as a rope, a ladder, a path, and other than that.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: its meaning is, "that I may reach, from the asbab of the heavens, asbab by which I may make a means to the sight of the God of Moses," whether those asbab are paths, or gates, or abodes, or other than that.

* *

His words: ﴿so that I may look upon the God of Moses﴾

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿fa-attali'a﴾. The majority of the readers of the regional centers recited it as "fa-attali'u" with a damma on the ayn, in conjunction with and as a coordination to His words ﴿I may reach the asbab﴾. It is reported that Humayd al-A'raj recited ﴿fa-attali'a﴾ with a fatha, as an answer (jawab) to "la'alli" (perhaps). al-Farra' mentioned that some Arabs recited to him:

"Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns / will let us overcome its afflictions / so that the soul may rest from its sighs."

[These are verses of mashtur rajaz. al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: His words "la'alli ablughu al-asbab fa-attali'" with the raf', returning it to His words "ablugh." Whoever makes it an answer to "la'alli" puts it in the nasb, and some readers recited it so. He said: some Arabs recited to me: "'Alla sarufu al-dahr...," the verses, and he put it in the nasb as an answer to "la'alla." The rajaz's composer is unknown. "'Al" is a dialectal form of "la'alla." al-Dawalat is the plural of dawla in wealth, and with a fatha in war; it is said both are one. "Yudilnana" is from al-idala, which means dominance. "Al-lamma" with a fatha is hardship, and it is the second object of "yudilnana." The evidence is in "fa-tastarih," where it is put in the nasb in answer to "la'alla," which is a particle of hope, as al-Farra' said. This is the correct view, because it is confirmed in the Qur'an: "Perhaps he would purify himself, or remember, and the reminder would benefit him." The zafarat are the plural of zafra, which is a single breath of sighing, namely a person filling his chest with air by inhaling, then exhaling and expelling it, and that is at grief and sorrow. The recitation which I do not allow other than is the raf' in this, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed I think he is a liar﴾

He says: "And indeed I think Moses is a liar in what he says and claims, that he has a Lord in the heaven who sent him to us."

* *

His words: ﴿And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And thus Allah made attractive to Pharaoh, when he transgressed and rebelled, the ugliness of his deed, until his soul made him believe in reaching the asbab of the heavens to look upon the God of Moses.

* *

His words: ﴿and he was averted from the way﴾

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited ﴿wa-suddu 'ani al-sabil﴾ with a damma on the sad, in the form of the passive voice (ma lam yusamma fa'iluh).

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and he was averted from the way﴾ he said: this was done to him; his evil deed was made attractive to him, and he was averted from the way.

Humayd, Abu 'Amr, and the majority of the readers of Basra recited "wa-sadda" with a fatha on the sad, meaning: Pharaoh turned away from the way of Allah with which Moses was sent, out of arrogance.

The correct statement on this is to say: both are two well-known recitations among the recitations of the regional centers, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct.

His words: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And the scheming of Pharaoh, by which he schemed to look upon the God of Moses, was nothing but in loss, the waste of wealth, and deception, because the expense he spent on the tower went in vain, and he gained nothing of what he intended by what he spent. That is the loss and the tabab.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾ he said: in loss.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words: ﴿in ruin﴾ he said: loss.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾: i.e., in misguidance and loss.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his words: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾: "al-Tabab and al-Dalal are one."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 36–37:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways (al-asbab)—the ways of the heavens—and look upon the God of Moses, though I think he is a liar." And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the way. And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Pharaoh said, when the believer from his family admonished him with what he admonished him and warned him against killing Moses, the prophet of Allah, and cautioned him of the might of Allah for his saying "I will kill him," to his vizier, the evil vizier Haman: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the asbab,﴾ meaning: a building.

We have already explained the meaning of al-sarh (tower) earlier, with its evidences, in a manner that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

﴿That I may reach the asbab﴾: the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-asbab in this place. Some of them said: "The asbab of the heavens" means their paths.

Those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Israel, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿asbab al-samawat﴾ he said: the paths of the heavens.

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿I may reach the asbab, the asbab of the heavens﴾ he said: the paths of the heavens.

Others said: What is meant by the asbab of the heavens is the gates of the heavens.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build for me a tower"﴾ — and he was the first to build with this baked brick and fire it — ﴿that I may reach the asbab, the asbab of the heavens﴾: i.e., the gates of the heavens.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is the abode of the heaven.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: ﴿that I may reach the asbab, the asbab of the heavens﴾: he said: the abode of the heaven.

We have already explained earlier that the sabab is everything by which one makes a means to reach what is sought, such as a rope, a ladder, a path, and other than that.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: its meaning is, "that I may reach, from the asbab of the heavens, asbab by which I may make a means to the sight of the God of Moses," whether those asbab are paths, or gates, or abodes, or other than that.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿fa-attali'a﴾. The majority of the readers of the regional centers recited it as "fa-attali'u" with a damma on the ayn, in conjunction with and as a coordination to His words ﴿I may reach the asbab﴾. It is reported that Humayd al-A'raj recited ﴿fa-attali'a﴾ with a fatha, as an answer (jawab) to "la'alli" (perhaps). al-Farra' mentioned that some Arabs recited to him:

"Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns / will let us overcome its afflictions / so that the soul may rest from its sighs."

[These are verses of mashtur rajaz. al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: His words "la'alli ablughu al-asbab fa-attali'" with the raf', returning it to His words "ablugh." Whoever makes it an answer to "la'alli" puts it in the nasb, and some readers recited it so. He said: some Arabs recited to me: "'Alla sarufu al-dahr...," the verses, and he put it in the nasb as an answer to "la'alla." The rajaz's composer is unknown. "'Al" is a dialectal form of "la'alla." al-Dawalat is the plural of dawla in wealth, and with a fatha in war; it is said both are one. "Yudilnana" is from al-idala, which means dominance. "Al-lamma" with a fatha is hardship, and it is the second object of "yudilnana." The evidence is in "fa-tastarih," where it is put in the nasb in answer to "la'alla," which is a particle of hope, as al-Farra' said. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 38–39:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct. O my people, this worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement."﴾

Exalted is He, He says, informing about the believer in Allah from the family of Pharaoh: ﴿And he who believed said﴾ from the people of Pharaoh, to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct.﴾ That is, "If you follow me and accept from me what I tell you, I will make clear to you the path of righteousness, which, if you take it and travel it, you will be guided, and that is the religion of Allah with which Moses was sent."

He says: ﴿Indeed, this worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment.﴾ That is, he said to his people: "This worldly life, the hasty one that has been hastened to you in this abode, is nothing but enjoyment through which you take pleasure until a term you will reach, after which you die and it departs from you." ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the abode of settlement.﴾ That is, "And indeed the next abode, which is the abode of settlement in which you will remain, neither dying nor departing from you." That is, "So for it work, and it alone seek."

And in accordance with what we have said concerning the meaning of His saying, ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the abode of settlement,﴾ the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾: "Paradise is settled with its people, and the Fire is settled with its people."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 38–39:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct. O my people, this worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement."﴾

That is, "So for it work, and it alone seek."

And in accordance with what we have said concerning the meaning of His saying, ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the abode of settlement,﴾ the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾: "Paradise is settled with its people, and the Fire is settled with its people."

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, being provided for therein without account﴾.

He says: whoever acts in disobedience to Allah in this worldly life, Allah will not recompense him in the Hereafter except with an evil like it, meaning that He will punish him with it. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, He says: and whoever acts in obedience to Allah in this world, complies with His command, and refrains in it from what He has forbidden, whether man or woman, ﴿while being a believer in Allah﴾, ﴿those will enter Paradise﴾, He says: those among the servants of Allah who do that will enter Paradise in the Hereafter.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾, meaning shirk; "the evil deed (al-sayyi'ah) according to Qatadah is shirk." ﴿And whoever does righteousness﴾, meaning good, ﴿whether male or female while being a believer﴾.

And His words: ﴿They are provided for therein without account﴾

He says: Allah will provide them in Paradise with its fruits, and with its bounties and pleasures, without account.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They are provided for therein without account﴾, he said: "No, by Allah, there is neither measure nor scale among you."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, what is [the matter] with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?﴾ (41) ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.﴾ (42)

Says the Exalted, relating the speech of this believer to his people, who were disbelievers: ﴿What is [the matter] with me that I call you to salvation﴾ from the punishment and retribution of Allah, by believing in Him, following His messenger Musa, and affirming what he has brought you from his Lord, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾. He means: while you call me to the deeds of the people of the Fire.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Among those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿What is [the matter] with me that I call you to salvation﴾, he said: "Belief in Allah."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿What is [the matter] with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire﴾, he said: "This was a believer from the family of Pharaoh. They were calling him to their religion and to remaining with them."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge﴾

He means: and to associate with Allah in worship idols, of which I know no [basis] that it is fitting for me to worship them or to associate them with the worship of Allah, for Allah has not permitted me to do so by any report or by reason.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿while I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver﴾

He means: and I call you to worship the Exalted in Might in His retribution against those who disbelieve in Him, whom nothing can prevent when He takes vengeance upon an enemy of His, and the Perpetual Forgiver to whoever repents to Him after disobeying Him, by His pardoning him, so nothing harms him along with His pardon of him. He means: so worship the one whose attribute is this, not that which has neither harm nor benefit with Him.

The Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿Undoubtedly, what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter, and indeed our return is to God, and indeed the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾ (40:43)

He says: Truly, that to which you call me, of idols, has no call (no answer to those who call on it) in this world or in the Hereafter, because it is an inanimate object that does not speak and does not understand anything.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿has no call in this world﴾, he said: The idol is nothing.

* *

And His words: ﴿and indeed our return is to God﴾

He says: And indeed our return and our turning after our death is to God. ﴿And indeed the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾: he says: And indeed the polytheists who associate others with God and who exceed His limits, the killers of souls which God has forbidden to kill, are the companions of the Fire of Hell at our return to God.

The interpreters have said the like of what we have said on this, though they differed on the meaning of "the transgressors" (al-musrifun) in this place. Some of them said: They are those who shed blood without right.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and indeed the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, he said: They are those who shed blood without right.

'Ali ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿and indeed the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, he said: They are those who shed blood without right.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and indeed the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, he said: God named them transgressors: Pharaoh and those with him.

Others said: They are the polytheists.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and indeed the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾: that is, the polytheists. We have already explained the meaning of excess (al-israf) earlier, sufficiently, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

We chose what we chose in interpreting this passage because the speaker of this statement was addressing Pharaoh and his people; Pharaoh was meant by it for his disbelief and for what he intended of killing Musa, and Pharaoh was haughty, rebellious in disbelief, and a shedder of blood which he was forbidden to shed, and all of that is excess. Therefore we chose the interpretation that we chose.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 44–45:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So you will remember what I say to you. And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.﴾ (40:44) ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and the terrible torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh.﴾ (40:45)

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying, reporting the speech of the believer from the family of Pharaoh to Pharaoh and his people: "So you will remember, O people, when you witness the punishment of Allah descending upon you, and you encounter what you have encountered, the truth of what I say and the reality of what I inform you of: that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire."

As related:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿So you will remember what I say to you﴾. I said to him: "Is that in the Hereafter?" He said: "Yes."

* *

And His words: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾

He says: "I surrender my affair to Allah, I make it His, and I rely upon Him, for He is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him."

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ He said: "I make my affair to Allah."

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾

He says: "Indeed, Allah is Knowing of the affairs of His servants, of who among them is obedient and who is disobedient to Him, and who deserves the goodly reward and who merits the evil punishment."

* *

And His words: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "So Allah repelled from this believer from the family of Pharaoh, by his faith and his affirmation of His messenger Musa, the harm of what Pharaoh was inflicting upon those who opposed him of torment and trial, and He delivered him from it."

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿the evils of what they plotted﴾ He said: "He was a Copt from the people of Pharaoh, and he was saved along with Musa." He said: "It was mentioned to us that on that day he was walking before Musa, and he was saying: 'Where have you been commanded, O Prophet of Allah?' He says: 'Before you.' So the believer says to him: 'And is there before me anything but the sea?' Musa says: 'No, by Allah, I have not lied, nor have I been lied to.' Then he walks for an hour and says: 'Where have you been commanded, O Prophet of Allah?' He says: 'Before you.' He says: 'And is there before me anything but the sea?' He says: 'No, by Allah, I have not lied, nor have I been lied to.' Until he reached the sea and struck it with his staff, and it split into twelve paths, one path for each tribe."

* *

And His words: ﴿And the terrible torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh﴾

He says: "And it descended upon the family of Pharaoh and became binding upon them; and by the family of Pharaoh in this place is meant his followers and those obedient to him from among his people."

As related:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And the terrible torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh﴾ He said: "The people of Pharaoh."

And by His words: ﴿the terrible torment﴾ is meant what displeased them of the punishment of Allah, and that is the Fire of Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 44–45:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So you will remember what I say to you. And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.﴾ (40:44) ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and the terrible torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh.﴾ (40:45)

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying, reporting the speech of the believer from the family of Pharaoh to Pharaoh and his people: "So you will remember, O people, when you witness the punishment of Allah descending upon you, and you encounter what you have encountered, the truth of what I say and the reality of what I inform you of: that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire."

As related:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿So you will remember what I say to you﴾. I said to him: "Is that in the Hereafter?" He said: "Yes."

* *

And His words: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾

He says: "I surrender my affair to Allah, I make it His, and I rely upon Him, for He is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him."

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ He said: "I make my affair to Allah."

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾

He says: "Indeed, Allah is Knowing of the affairs of His servants, of who among them is obedient and who is disobedient to Him, and who deserves the goodly reward and who merits the evil punishment."

* *

And His words: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "So Allah repelled from this believer from the family of Pharaoh, by his faith and his affirmation of His messenger Musa, the harm of what Pharaoh was inflicting upon those who opposed him of torment and trial, and He delivered him from it."

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿the evils of what they plotted﴾ He said: "He was a Copt from the people of Pharaoh, and he was saved along with Musa." He said: "It was mentioned to us that on that day he was walking before Musa, and he was saying: 'Where have you been commanded, O Prophet of Allah?' He says: 'Before you.' So the believer says to him: 'And is there before me anything but the sea?' Musa says: 'No, by Allah, I have not lied, nor have I been lied to.' Then he walks for an hour and says: 'Where have you been commanded, O Prophet of Allah?' He says: 'Before you.' He says: 'And is there before me anything but the sea?' He says: 'No, by Allah, I have not lied, nor have I been lied to.' Until he reached the sea and struck it with his staff, and it split into twelve paths, one path for each tribe."

* *

And His words: ﴿And the terrible torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh﴾

He says: "And it descended upon the family of Pharaoh and became binding upon them; and by the family of Pharaoh in this place is meant his followers and those obedient to him from among his people."

As related:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And the terrible torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh﴾ He said: "The people of Pharaoh."

And by His words: ﴿the terrible torment﴾ is meant what displeased them of the punishment of Allah, and that is the Fire of Hell.

Commentary on the verse: "The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening. And on the day the Hour is established: 'Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment.'" (40:46)

The meaning of His saying, the Exalted, explaining the evil of the punishment that befell these wretched people of Pharaoh's folk, that which encompassed them of the evil punishment of God: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it﴾. When they perished and God drowned them, their souls were placed in the bellies of black birds, and they are exposed to the Fire twice every day ﴿morning and evening﴾ until the Hour is established.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Qays, from al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, who said: The souls of the people of Pharaoh are in the bellies of black birds; they go forth and return upon the Fire, and that is their exposure.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: It has reached me that the souls of Pharaoh's people are in the bellies of black birds, exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Hour is established.

Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Muhammad al-Fazari al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i, and a man asked him, saying: "May God have mercy on you, we have seen birds coming out of the sea taking the direction of the west, white, in flocks upon flocks, whose number none knows but God; and when evening comes, the like of them return black." He said: "And did you perceive that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Those birds have in their crops the souls of the people of Pharaoh; they are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, then they return to their nests with their plumage burnt and turned black; then white feathers grow upon them at night, and the black ones fall out; then they go forth again, and they are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, then they return to their nests. That is their practice in this world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God says: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾." They said: And they used to say: they were six hundred thousand fighting men.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Harmala narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Humayd, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "In the Hereafter there is no night and no midday; there is only morning and evening, and that is in the Qur'an concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾, and likewise He said to the people of Paradise: ﴿and they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾."

It was also said: what is meant by that is that they are exposed upon their dwellings in the Fire, to be punished morning and evening.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾, he said: They are exposed to it in the morning and evening; it is said to them: "O people of Pharaoh, this is your dwelling," as rebuke, vengeance, and humiliation for them.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿morning and evening﴾, he said: "That is what the world was."

The most correct of the sayings on this, in my view, is to say: God has informed that the people of Pharaoh are exposed to the Fire morning and evening. It is permissible that this exposure to the Fire be in the manner we mentioned from al-Hudhayl and those who said as he did, and that it be as Qatadah said. There is no report establishing with proof which of these is meant, so there is nothing in this except what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates, namely that they are exposed to the Fire morning and evening. The root of "ghuduww" (morning) and "ashiyy" (evening) is that they are verbal nouns that have been made into time expressions.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say about this: it is only a verbal noun, as you say: "I came to him at dark (ẓalaman)"; he made it an adverb while it is a verbal noun. He said: If you said: "Your appointment is ghadwatan (morning)" or "Your appointment is ẓalām," putting it in the nominative, as you say "Your appointment is Friday," it would not be good, because these verbal nouns and what resembles them, such as saḥar (pre-dawn), are only used as adverbs; and the adverbial construction as a whole is not fully declinable. The grammarians of Kufa said: in these time expressions, although they are verbal nouns, nothing has been heard except the accusative construction, such as "Your appointment is morning" and "Your appointment is dawn and dusk," just as the Exalted said: ﴿Its morning journey is a month and its evening journey is a month﴾, where it is in the nominative. They mentioned that they heard: "Indeed the cloak (ṭaylasān) is two months" [the ṭaylasān being a garment that scholars and nobles would place around their necks and over their shoulders to ward off cold, meaning the period of wearing it is two months]. They said: In indefinite time expressions nothing has been heard in the nominative except their saying: "Indeed your generosity is at times," and they said: it is permissible because it means: "Indeed your generosity is the period after period," and since its interpretation is the construction with a genitive, it is put in the accusative.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment."﴾

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of readers of Hijaz and Iraq, except Asim and Abu Amr, recited ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, admit the people of Pharaoh﴾ with a fatha on the alif of "adkhulu" both in connection and in pause, meaning a command to admit them to the Fire. When it is recited thus, "al" is in the accusative by being the object of "adkhulu." Asim and Abu Amr recited it as "adkhilu" (with a damma), with the alif elided in connection and dropped in the wording, and with a damma when begun after pausing on "al-sa'ah." Whoever recites it this way, "al" in their reading is in the accusative by address, since the meaning of the speech in their reading is: "Enter, O people of Pharaoh, the most severe punishment."

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is to say that both are well-known readings, close in meaning, each recited by a group of readers; so whichever of them the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the speech then is: "And on the day the Hour is established, it will be said to the people of Pharaoh: 'Enter, O people of Pharaoh, the most severe punishment'" — this according to the reading that connects the alif of "udkhulu" and does not cut it; and its meaning according to the other reading is: "And on the day the Hour is established, God will say to His angels: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 47–48:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And mention when they will dispute within the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were to you followers, so can you avert from us a portion of the Fire?"﴾ [40:47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [40:48]

His Exalted remembrance says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, suppressing grief﴾ [40:18]. ﴿And when they dispute within the Fire﴾: it means, "when they argue with one another in the Fire." By this He means: when those among the polytheists of his people whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to warn dispute within the Fire, the weak among them, namely those who followed others in associating partners with Allah, will say ﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾, saying to their leaders who led them into error: "Indeed, we were followers of you in disbelief in Allah in the worldly life." ﴿So can you avert﴾ today ﴿from us a portion of the Fire﴾, meaning a share, that you may lighten it for us. For we used to hasten to love you in the world, and we came to you [seeking your guidance]; had it not been for you, we would have been believers in the world, and this affliction would not have befallen us today. The word "tabaʿ" (followers) may be singular or plural, according to the view of some grammarians of Basra; according to some grammarians of Kufa, it is a plural with no singular, since it is like a verbal noun. He said: "If you wish, its singular may be tābiʿ, so it would be like khāʾil and khawal, and ghāʾib and ghayb."

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that it is a plural whose singular is tābiʿ, though it may also be permissible for it to be singular, in which case its plural would be atbāʿ. So the leaders who were followed answered them with what Allah reported of them; ﴿Those who were arrogant said﴾, namely the leaders who were followed in error in the worldly life: "Indeed, we and you, O people, are all in this Fire, eternally abiding, with no deliverance for us from it." ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants﴾ by the decisive division of His judgment, so He has settled the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire; thus neither are we emerging from the affliction we are in, nor are they moving from the bliss they have. The word ﴿kull﴾ is in the nominative by His saying ﴿fīhā﴾ (in it), and it was not put in the accusative as a qualifier.

There has been disagreement about the permissibility of the accusative in this construction in speech. Some grammarians of Basra used to say: if "kull" is not followed by a genitive noun, then the agreement (as a qualifier) is not permissible. Some grammarians of Kufa used to say: that is permissible both with ellipsis and without ellipsis, because when its referent is omitted it is sufficient in itself. We have already clarified the correct view on this matter earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 49–50:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ ﴿They will say, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?" They will say, "Yes." They will say, "Then call," but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: The people of Hell say to their keepers and guardians, seeking their help against the great affliction they are in, and hoping that they will find some relief from them: ﴿Call upon your Lord﴾ for us ﴿to lighten for us a day﴾, meaning one day, that is, the length of one day of the days of this world, ﴿of the punishment﴾ in which we are. We only say that the meaning of this is the length of a day of the days of this world, because the Hereafter is a day in which there is no night, so it would not be said: "lighten for them one day."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They will say, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?"﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: The keepers of Hell will say to them: "Did there not come to you, in the world, your messengers with clear proofs of the Oneness of God, so that you would declare Him one, believe in Him, and disavow what is worshipped besides Him of gods?" They will say: "Yes, indeed, our messengers came to us with that."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They will say, "Then call"﴾

His saying, may His praise be exalted: The keepers said to them: "Then call upon your Lord, whom the messengers came to you calling you to believe in."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾

He says: They have called, but their supplication is only in error, because it is a supplication that does not benefit them and is not answered for them; rather it will be said to them: ﴿"Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me."﴾

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾ (51) ﴿the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ (52).

One says: What is the meaning of ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾, when we know that some of them were killed by their enemies and mutilated, such as Sha'ya (Isaiah), Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah), and their likes? And some of them were resolved to be killed by their people, and the best of their conditions was that they escaped from them until they parted from them, saved by their own selves, such as Ibrahim, who migrated to al-Sham from his land, separating from his people, and 'Isa, who was raised up to heaven when his people wanted to kill him. So where is the help which He informed us that He would give to His messengers and to the believers in Him in the worldly life, when these are His prophets, to whom has befallen from their people what you know, and they were not helped against those who afflicted them with what they afflicted them with?

It is said: For His words, ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾, there are two aspects, both of which are correct in meaning. One of them is that its meaning is: Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life, either by raising them above those who denied Us and granting them victory over them, until they overpower them with dominance and humiliate them with victory in abasement, as He did in this regard with Dawud and Sulayman, giving them the kingdom and authority by which they subdued every disbeliever, and as He did with Muhammad ﷺ by making him prevail over those of his people who denied him; or by avenging Ourselves upon those who opposed them and defied them by destroying them and saving the messengers from those who denied and opposed them, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, did with Nuh and his people, by drowning his people and saving him from them, and as He did with Musa and Fir'awn and his people, when He destroyed them by drowning and saved Musa and those who believed in him from the Children of Israel and others, and the like of that; or by avenging Ourselves in the worldly life upon their deniers after the death of Our messenger, following their destruction, as We did in helping Sha'ya after his death, by empowering over his killers those whom We empowered until We took vengeance upon his killers through them, and as We did with the killers of Yahya, by empowering Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) over them until We took vengeance through him upon his killers, and as Our help to 'Isa against those who intended to kill him by the Romans, until We destroyed them through them. This is one of its two aspects. Some of the people of interpretation directed the meaning of this to this aspect.

Among those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾: The prophets and the believers were killed in the world while they were victorious, and that is because that nation which does that to the prophets and the believers does not depart until Allah raises up a people by whom He takes vengeance on those of them who were killed.

The other aspect: that this statement is in the form of a report about all of the messengers and believers, and the intended meaning is one, so the interpretation of the statement then is: Indeed, We will surely help Our messenger Muhammad ﷺ and those who believed in him in the worldly life, and on the day when the witnesses stand, as we have explained previously, that the Arabs express a report in the plural form while the intended meaning is singular when they do not single out a specific individual for the report.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth], the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾. The majority of the readers of Madina and Kufa recited ﴿wa-yawma yaqumu﴾ with the yā' (yaqumu), and also yanfa'u with the yā'. Some of the people of Makka and some of the readers of Basra recited "taqumu" with the tā', and "tanfa'u" with the tā'.

The correct view regarding this is that both are two well-known recitations with one meaning, so whichever of the two a reader recites is correct.

We have previously explained that the Arabs mention the verb for a man and make it feminine when the subject has been mentioned before in a way that makes its repetition unnecessary.

By His words: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾ is meant: the day when the witnesses stand, from among the angels, the prophets and the believers, against the nations that denied their messengers, bearing witness that the messengers had conveyed to them the messages of their Lord, and that the nations denied them. And al-ashhad (the witnesses) is the plural of shahid (witness), as al-ashraf is the plural of sharif (noble).

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said in this regard.

Among those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾: from among the angels of Allah and His prophets, and the believers in Him.

Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾: He said: the angels.

* *

His words: ﴿the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: That is a day on which the excuse of the people of polytheism will not benefit them, because they do not make excuses, and if they do make excuses, they make them only with falsehood; that is because Allah had already given them an excuse in the world and followed up the proofs upon them therein, so they have no proof in the Hereafter except to cling to lying by saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾.

* *

His words: ﴿and for them is the curse﴾

He says: For the wrongdoers is the curse, which is distance from the mercy of Allah. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾: He says: For them, along with the curse from Allah, is the worst of what is in the Hereafter, which is the painful punishment.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾ (51) ﴿the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ (52).

One says: What is the meaning of ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾, when we know that some of them were killed by their enemies and mutilated, such as Sha'ya (Isaiah), Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah), and their likes? And some of them were resolved to be killed by their people, and the best of their conditions was that they escaped from them until they parted from them, saved by their own selves, such as Ibrahim, who migrated to al-Sham from his land, separating from his people, and 'Isa, who was raised up to heaven when his people wanted to kill him. So where is the help which He informed us that He would give to His messengers and to the believers in Him in the worldly life, when these are His prophets, to whom has befallen from their people what you know, and they were not helped against those who afflicted them with what they afflicted them with?

It is said: For His words, ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾, there are two aspects, both of which are correct in meaning. One of them is that its meaning is: Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life, either by raising them above those who denied Us and granting them victory over them, until they overpower them with dominance and humiliate them with victory in abasement, as He did in this regard with Dawud and Sulayman, giving them the kingdom and authority by which they subdued every disbeliever, and as He did with Muhammad ﷺ by making him prevail over those of his people who denied him; or by avenging Ourselves upon those who opposed them and defied them by destroying them and saving the messengers from those who denied and opposed them, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, did with Nuh and his people, by drowning his people and saving him from them, and as He did with Musa and Fir'awn and his people, when He destroyed them by drowning and saved Musa and those who believed in him from the Children of Israel and others, and the like of that; or by avenging Ourselves in the worldly life upon their deniers after the death of Our messenger, following their destruction, as We did in helping Sha'ya after his death, by empowering over his killers those whom We empowered until We took vengeance upon his killers through them, and as We did with the killers of Yahya, by empowering Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) over them until We took vengeance through him upon his killers, and as Our help to 'Isa against those who intended to kill him by the Romans, until We destroyed them through them. This is one of its two aspects. Some of the people of interpretation directed the meaning of this to this aspect.

Among those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾: The prophets and the believers were killed in the world while they were victorious, and that is because that nation which does that to the prophets and the believers does not depart until Allah raises up a people by whom He takes vengeance on those of them who were killed.

The other aspect: that this statement is in the form of a report about all of the messengers and believers, and the intended meaning is one, so the interpretation of the statement then is: Indeed, We will surely help Our messenger Muhammad ﷺ and those who believed in him in the worldly life, and on the day when the witnesses stand, as we have explained previously, that the Arabs express a report in the plural form while the intended meaning is singular when they do not single out a specific individual for the report.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth], the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾. The majority of the readers of Madina and Kufa recited ﴿wa-yawma yaqumu﴾ with the yā' (yaqumu), and also yanfa'u with the yā'. Some of the people of Makka and some of the readers of Basra recited "taqumu" with the tā', and "tanfa'u" with the tā'.

The correct view regarding this is that both are two well-known recitations with one meaning, so whichever of the two a reader recites is correct.

We have previously explained that the Arabs mention the verb for a man and make it feminine when the subject has been mentioned before in a way that makes its repetition unnecessary.

By His words: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾ is meant: the day when the witnesses stand, from among the angels, the prophets and the believers, against the nations that denied their messengers, bearing witness that the messengers had conveyed to them the messages of their Lord, and that the nations denied them. And al-ashhad (the witnesses) is the plural of shahid (witness), as al-ashraf is the plural of sharif (noble).

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said in this regard.

Among those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾: from among the angels of Allah and His prophets, and the believers in Him.

Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand [forth]﴾: He said: the angels.

* *

His words: ﴿the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: That is a day on which the excuse of the people of polytheism will not benefit them, because they do not make excuses, and if they do make excuses, they make them only with falsehood; that is because Allah had already given them an excuse in the world and followed up the proofs upon them therein, so they have no proof in the Hereafter except to cling to lying by saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾.

* *

His words: ﴿and for them is the curse﴾

He says: For the wrongdoers is the curse, which is distance from the mercy of Allah. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾: He says: For them, along with the curse from Allah, is the worst of what is in the Hereafter, which is the painful punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 53–54:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave Moses guidance and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ [53] ﴿as guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾ [54] ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning﴾ [55].

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿And We gave Moses﴾ the clarification of the truth with which We sent him, just as We gave that to Muhammad, and Pharaoh and his people denied it, just as Quraysh denied Muhammad. ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ means: and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Torah, so We taught it to them and sent it down to them. ﴿Guidance﴾ means a clarification of the matter of their religion and of the obligations We imposed upon them through its precepts. ﴿And a reminder for people of understanding﴾ means: and a reminder from Us to those among them who possess intellect and reason, through it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So be patient, O Muhammad, regarding the command of your Lord, and persist in what He sent you with of the message, and convey to your people and to those you were commanded to convey to what has been sent down to you. And be certain of the reality of Allah's promise that He made you, of supporting you and supporting those who believed you and had faith in you, against those who denied you and rejected what you brought from your Lord. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, with no breach in it, and He will surely fulfill it for him. ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ means: and ask Him to forgive your sins and pardon you for them. ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise﴾ means: and pray with gratitude from you to your Lord. ﴿In the evening﴾ this refers to the period from the decline of the sun until the night. ﴿And the morning﴾ this refers to the period from the rising of the second dawn until the rising of the sun. Some people have directed "the morning" to mean from sunrise until the height of forenoon, and the passing of the time of forenoon, but the well-known view among the Arabs is the first.

The grammarians differed regarding the reason for conjoining "al-ibkar" (the morning) with the preposition "bi" (in), since its entry before it is not good, whereas it is good before "al-ashi" (the evening). Some grammarians of Basra said: the meaning of that is: "and exalt your Lord with praise in the evening and in the morning." And he said: it is said "bi-l-dar Zayd" meaning "fi l-dar Zayd" (Zayd is in the house). Another said: it was only said in this way because the meaning of the statement is: pray with praise at these two times and in these two times, so the preposition enters one of them with both.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 55–56:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ (40:56)

The Exalted says: Indeed, those who dispute with you, O Muhammad, concerning what you have brought them from your Lord of the signs ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, meaning: without any proof having come to them from Allah for their disputing with you about them. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾, meaning: what is in their breasts is nothing but pride, by which they are arrogant toward following you and accepting the truth you have brought them, out of envy of the favour Allah has given you and the honour with which He has honoured you through prophethood. ﴿They will never attain it﴾, meaning: what they envy you for is a matter they will not reach or obtain, because it is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and it is not something attained through wishful thinking. It has also been said that its meaning is: there is nothing in their breasts except greatness, which they will never attain, because Allah will humiliate them.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿there is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾, he said: "Greatness."

And the people of interpretation have said in the same manner as what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them﴾.

Those who said this:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them﴾, "No authority has come to them with that."

And His words: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾

The Exalted says: So seek help from Allah, O Muhammad, against the evil of these people who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority, and against the pride that something of it might arise in your heart. ﴿Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾, meaning: Indeed, Allah is the Hearer of what these disputers say concerning the signs of Allah and others' speech, and the Seer of what their limbs bear, nothing of that being hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 57–58:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Certainly, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The creation and origination of the heavens and the earth without any prior matter is greater, O people, in your estimation, if you consider the creation of mankind and their origination without any prior matter to be great. But most of mankind do not know that the creation of all of that is easy for God.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the wrongdoer. Little do you take heed﴾

"The blind" is the one who sees nothing, and this is a likeness of the disbeliever who does not contemplate God's proofs with his eyes, so that he reflects upon them and takes lesson from them, and thereby knows His oneness and His power to create whatever He wills, and believes in Him and affirms Him. "The seeing" is the one who sees with his eyes what is present before them and perceives it, and this is a likeness of the believer who sees God's proofs with his eyes, reflects upon them and takes admonition, and knows what they indicate of the oneness of their Maker, His great dominion, and His power to create what He wills. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Likewise, the disbeliever and the believer are not equal. ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Likewise, those who believe in God and His Messenger and obey their Lord are not equal to the wrongdoer, who is the one who disbelieves in his Lord, disobeys Him, and opposes His command. ﴿Little do you take heed﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Little do you take heed, O people, of God's proofs, so that you might consider and be admonished. He means: If you remembered His signs and considered them, you would know the error of what you persist in, namely your denial of God's power to bring back to life those of His creation who have perished after their perishing, and to restore them to their lives after their deaths, and you would know the ugliness of your associating others in the worship of your Lord.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿tatadhakkarun﴾ (you take heed). The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it as "yatadhakkarun" with the ya (third person, as a report), while the majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as ﴿tatadhakkarun﴾ with the ta (second person, as direct address). The view on this is that both recitations are correct.
