**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 40, verses 59–60**

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿Indeed, the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt in it, but most of the people do not believe﴾ (59) ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation"﴾ (60):**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, the Hour, in which God will revive the dead for reward and punishment, is coming, O people, and there is no doubt about its coming. That is, be certain of its coming, and that you will be resurrected after your death and recompensed for your deeds, so repent to your Lord. ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾: that is, but most of the Quraysh do not believe in its coming.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me"﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And your Lord, O people, says: "Call upon Me," that is: worship Me and devote worship sincerely to Me, rather than what you worship besides Me, such as idols, images, and other things. ﴿I will respond to you﴾: that is, I will answer your supplication, so I will pardon you and have mercy on you.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., exegesis) have said what we have said about this.

**Mention of those who said that:**

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾: he said: "Declare Me to be One, and I will forgive you."

* Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Zirr, from Yusay' al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me"﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Zirr, from Yusay' al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Supplication is worship," and ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾ ... the verse.

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Zirr, from Yusay', who said: Abu Musa said: Thus said Ghundar, from Sa'id, from Mansur, from Zirr, from Yusay', from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, supplication is worship," and ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Zirr, from Yusay', from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it.

* al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn al-Araf al-Bahili narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Jahada, from Yusay' al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my worship is my supplication." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me"﴾, and he said: "[Worship] here means [supplication to] Me."

* Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Ammara narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: [Someone] said to Anas: "O Abu Hamza, has it reached you that supplication is half of worship?" He said: "No, rather it is all of worship."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Mansur informed us, from Zirr, from Yusay' al-Hadrami, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," then he recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me"﴾.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from al-Ash'ari, who said: It was said to Sufyan: "Supplicate to God." He said: "Abandoning sins is supplication."

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾

He says: Indeed, those who magnify themselves against singling Me out in worship, and singling out divinity for Me, ﴿will enter Hell in humiliation﴾: meaning, [they will enter it] abased. We have already explained the meaning of "dakhir" (humiliation) earlier, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

It has been said that the meaning of His words ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾ is: those who are too proud to supplicate to Me.

**Mention of those who said that:**

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾, who said: "[That is,] to supplicate to Me."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿dakhirin﴾, who said: "Abased."

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Zirr, from Yusay', from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾

He says: Indeed, those who magnify themselves against singling Me out in worship, and singling out divinity for Me, ﴿will enter Hell in humiliation﴾: meaning, [they will enter it] abased. We have already explained the meaning of "dakhir" (humiliation) earlier, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

It has been said that the meaning of His words ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾ is: those who are too proud to supplicate to Me.

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you, that you may rest therein, and the day to see by. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: Allah is the One who alone is fit to be worshipped, and to whom worship alone is due, the One whose attribute is that He made for you, O people, the night as a resting place, so that you may rest therein, ceasing from the movement and exertion of seeking livelihood and from the means by which you busied yourselves during your day. ﴿And the day to see by﴾: He made the day bright for the one who exerts himself therein in seeking his livelihood and pursuing his needs, as a blessing from Him to you by that. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind﴾: that is, indeed Allah is bountiful to you, O people, with a bounty for which there is no equal. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾: that is, but most of them do not thank Him by obedience to Him, by sincerely affirming His divinity and worshipping Him, and they have no prior favour toward Him by which they would deserve thanks from Him for it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 40, verses 62–65**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿That is God, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but Him. So how are you deluded?﴾ (62) ﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of God.﴾ (63)

He, exalted is His mention, says: He who did these deeds and bestowed these blessings upon you, O people, is God, your Owner and the one who manages your affairs. He is your Creator and the Creator of everything. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ means: there is no worshipped one deserving of worship besides Him. ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ means: in what direction do you turn, and where do you go away from Him, so that you worship other than Him?

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of God﴾

He says: just as you, O people, have turned away from Him and diverted from the truth to falsehood and from right guidance to error, so too turned away those who came before you among the nations, from the signs of God, meaning from the proofs and evidences of God, denying them and refusing to believe. He says: so you, O company of Quraysh, have followed their path and mounted their road of error.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿God is the One who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and fashioned you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is God, your Lord. Blessed is God, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ (64) ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but Him, so call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (65)

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿God﴾, to whom divinity belongs exclusively, O people, ﴿who made for you the earth﴾ upon whose surface you dwell as inhabitants, ﴿a resting place﴾ on which you settle and over which you live, ﴿and the sky a canopy﴾: He built it, raised it above you without pillars that you can see, for your benefit and for the sustenance of your worldly life until you reach your appointed terms. ﴿And fashioned you and perfected your forms﴾ means: He created you and made your creation excellent. ﴿And provided you with good things﴾ means: He provided you with lawful sustenance and delicious foods and drinks.

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is God, your Lord﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: the One who did these deeds and bestowed these blessings upon you, O people, is God, to whom alone divinity is fitting, and your Lord, to whom lordship alone is suitable, not one who neither benefits nor harms, neither creates nor provides. ﴿Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds﴾ means: blessed is God, the Owner of all creation, the jinn and mankind and all other kinds of creatures. ﴿He is the Living﴾ means: He is the Living who does not die, the Ever-living; everything other than Him has a life that ends and is not everlasting. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ means: there is no worshipped one with true right to be worshipped, and divinity is fitting for none but God, whose attributes are these attributes. ﴿So call upon Him, O people, sincere to Him in religion﴾ means: sincere to Him in obedience, affirming His divinity alone, and do not associate anything with Him in worship, whether idol or image, and do not set up rivals or equals to Him. ﴿Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ means: thanks belong to God, the Owner of all kinds of creatures, of angels, jinn, mankind and others, not to the gods and idols that own nothing and have no power to harm or benefit, but are themselves owned, and if any evil befalls them, they cannot ward it off from themselves.

A group of the people of knowledge used to command whoever said "There is no god but God" to follow it with: ﴿Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, interpreting this verse as a command from God to say it.

His saying, exalted is He, is addressed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people from Quraysh: ﴿Indeed, I have been forbidden﴾ O people ﴿to worship those you invoke besides Allah﴾ of gods and idols ﴿since the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord.﴾ He says: since the manifest signs have come to me from my Lord, and these are the verses of the Book of Allah which He sent down. * *

His saying: ﴿So they will come to know, when the shackles are on their necks and the chains﴾

This is a threat from Allah to the polytheists. His, may He be exalted, saying means: those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, who deny the Book, will come to know the reality of what you, O Muhammad, inform them of, and the truth of what they today deny of this Book, when shackles and chains are placed on their necks in Hell. The readers of the major cities recite "wa-s-salasilu" (and the chains) with the nominative, as a conjunction with "al-aghlal" (the shackles), according to the sense I have explained. It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he recited "wa-s-salasila yusbahuna" with the accusative "salasil" in the sense of "in the boiling water." It is also related from him that he used to say: it is actually "wa-hum fi s-salasil yusbahuna" (and they, in chains, are dragged). The scholars of Arabic do not permit the genitive of the noun when the governing particle is implied. Some of them said about this: if someone supposed that the meaning is "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains," then the genitive of "chains" would be permissible on this view, and he said: like it, what is referred back to the sense, the saying of the poet:

"The serpents have made peace with his foot, the cobra and the viper..."

[The verse is from the rajaz meter (Lisan: sh-j-ʿ). Al-shuja' is the serpent, and in a hadith: "On the Day of Resurrection his treasure will come as a bald serpent." Al-Ahmar recited: "The serpents have made peace...," the two verses. The accusative of "al-shuja'" and "al-af'wan" is in the sense of the statement, because when the serpents make peace with the foot, the foot has made peace with them, as if he said: the foot made peace with the serpents; then he made "al-af'wan" a substitute for them. End. Al-Farra said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 289): the accusative of "al-shuja'" and "al-hayyat" was previously nominative, because the meaning is that his foot made peace with the serpents and they made peace with it. When he needed the accusative for the rhyme, he made the verb from "the foot" fall upon the serpents. End.]

So the accusative of "al-shuja'" and "al-hayyat," which were previously nominative, because the meaning is: his foot made peace with the serpents and they made peace with it, and when he needed the accusative for the rhyme, he made the verb from the foot fall upon the serpents.

The correct reading in our view is that of the readers of the major cities, owing to the consensus of the authorities upon it, namely the nominative "salasilu," as a conjunction with what is in His saying: ﴿in their necks﴾, referring to the shackles.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will be dragged﴾

That is: these who denied in the world the Book will be dragged by the angels of punishment on the Day of Resurrection into the boiling water, which is that whose heat has ended and reached its extreme.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then in the Fire they will be kindled﴾

That is: then in the fire of Hell they will be burned. That is, Hell will be kindled with them, meaning it will be set ablaze with them.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said likewise.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿They will be kindled﴾: he said: the fire will be kindled with them.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then in the Fire they will be kindled﴾: he said: they will be burned in the Fire.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then in the Fire they will be kindled﴾: he said: they will be kindled in the Fire: it will be set ablaze upon them within it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then it will be said to them: Where is what you used to associate with Allah besides Him?﴾

That is: then it will be said: Where are those you used to associate, by worshipping them besides Allah, of your gods and idols, so that they may come to your aid and rescue you from the trial and punishment you are in? For the worshipped one helps whoever worships and serves him. This is said to them only as rebuke and reproach for what they did in the world of disbelief in Allah and obedience to Satan. The wretched ones then answer and say: "They have strayed from us," meaning: they have deviated from us, took other than our path, and left us in this trial. Rather, they have not strayed from us, but we did not use to call upon anything before, in the world: that is, we did not use to worship anything. Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Thus Allah misguides the disbelievers﴾, meaning: just as those whom they say strayed from them in Hell, what they used to worship in the world besides Allah of gods and idols, their gods and idols, so Allah misguides the people of disbelief in Him from Himself, from His mercy and worship, so He does not have mercy on them to save them from the Fire, nor does He come to their aid to lighten what they are in of trial.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

• Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Simsar narrated to us, saying: Ma'n ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir ibn Mismar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Yazid ibn Aban, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was sent after eight thousand prophets, among them four thousand from the Children of Israel.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from Utba ibn Utayba al-Basri al-Abdi, from Abu Sahl, from Wahb ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Sawr al-Azdi, from Salman, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah sent four thousand prophets."

• Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Tirmidhi narrated to me, saying: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Ibn Abd Allah ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding His words: ﴿Among them are those whom We have related to you and among them are those whom We have not related to you﴾, he said: Allah sent an Abyssinian servant as a prophet, and he is the one whom We have not related to you.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah﴾

He, the Exalted, says: We did not make it for any messenger, of those We sent before you — those whom We related to you and those whom We did not relate to you — to a nation, that he should bring his people a decisive sign between himself and them, except by Allah's permission to him to do so, so that he brings it to them. The Exalted says to His Prophet: For this reason We did not make it for you to bring your people whatever signs they ask of you without Our permission to you to do so, just as We did not make it for those before you of Our messengers except that We permit him to do so. ﴿So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth﴾ meaning with justice, which is that He saves His messengers and those who believe with them. ﴿And the falsifiers will lose [everything] at that time﴾ means: and those who made falsehood of their speech, fabricated against Allah, and claimed partners for Him will perish at that time.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verses 79–81:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the cattle, that you may ride upon some of them and eat of them. And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need within your breasts, and upon them and upon the ships you are carried.  And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, the One besides whom no divinity is fitting, O polytheists among the Quraysh who associate others with Him, ﴿who made for you the cattle﴾, namely the camels, cows, sheep, and horses, and other livestock that the people of Islam keep for riding or for food. ﴿That you may ride upon some of them﴾ means: the horses and donkeys. ﴿And of them you eat﴾ means: the camels, cows, and sheep. He said ﴿that you may ride upon some of them﴾, meaning: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them, so the second part has been omitted as being sufficiently indicated by the context.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for you in them are benefits﴾

This is because He made for you from their hides houses which you find light to carry on the day of your journey and the day of your residence, and from their wool, fur, and hair, furnishings and provision for a time.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need within your breasts﴾

He means: that you may reach, by means of the carrying on some of them, which are the camels, a need within your breasts, which you would not have reached were it not for them, except with great difficulty to yourselves, as His, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And they carry your burdens to a land you could not have reached except with the utmost difficulty to yourselves﴾. The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: (and that you may reach upon them a need within your breasts), meaning: the camels carry your burdens to a land.

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and that you may reach upon them a need within your breasts﴾, for your need, whatever it may be.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And upon them﴾

He means: and upon these camels and what resembles them of the riding livestock ﴿and upon the ships﴾, meaning: and upon the boats ﴿you are carried﴾. He says: We carry you upon these on land and upon these at sea. ﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, He says: and He shows you His proofs. ﴿So which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾ He says: So which of the proofs of Allah that He shows you, O people, in the heavens and the earth, do you deny the truth of, thereby lying, on account of their invalidity regarding the Oneness of Allah, and calling upon a god other than Him?

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than these and greater in strength and in monuments upon the earth, but what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these disputers over the signs of God among your people, O Muhammad, not travelled through the lands? Indeed, they are people who travel to Syria and Yemen, their journeys in winter and summer. Let them look at what they have trodden of the lands, at Our encounters with the nations We brought down before them, and let them see the punishment We inflicted upon them for their denial of Our messengers and their rejection of Our signs, and how the outcome of their denial was. ﴿They were more numerous than these﴾: that is, those who came before these deniers among Quraysh were more numerous in number than these, mightier in force, stronger in power, and more enduring in traces upon the earth, for they used to hew out houses from the mountains and build fortresses.

Mujahid used to say concerning this:

⁕ Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and monuments upon the earth﴾: the walking of their feet.

﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾: that is, when Our punishment and Our might came upon them, what they used to do in hewing houses in the mountains did not avail them, and that did not repel anything from them. Rather, they perished, all of them, and were destroyed. It has also been said that the meaning of His words ﴿did not avail them﴾ is: "what [thing] availed them?" According to this interpretation, the first "mā" must be in the accusative position and the second in the nominative position. The meaning is: so for these disputers among your people, O Muhammad, there is a lesson in those [nations] if they would take heed, and an admonition if they would be admonished; and Our punishment, when it descends upon a people who are criminals, is not repelled by any repeller and not prevented by any preventer, and it will befall them if they do not turn back to believing you.

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they exulted in the knowledge they had, and there encompassed them that which they had been mocking﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: When these nations who came before Quraysh, who denied their messengers, had their messengers come to them—the messengers whom God sent to them—with clear proofs, meaning: with evident arguments from Him, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿they exulted in the knowledge they had﴾. He says: they exulted, out of ignorance on their part, in the knowledge they had, and they said: "We will not be resurrected, and God will not punish us."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God ﴿they exulted in the knowledge they had﴾: He said: Their saying: "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished, and we will not be resurrected."

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, ﴿they exulted in the knowledge they had﴾: with their ignorance.

* *

And His words: ﴿and there encompassed them that which they had been mocking﴾

He says: There encompassed them of God's punishment that which they had been asking their messengers to hasten, mockingly and derisively.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and there encompassed them that which they had been mocking﴾: what their messengers brought them of the truth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 40, verse 84–85:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ (84)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: When these disbelieving nations saw Our might, meaning the punishment of Allah which their messengers had promised them, had descended upon them.

As related:

Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿So when they saw Our might﴾: He said, "The vengeances that descended upon them."

* *

As for His saying ﴿They said, "We believe in Allah alone"﴾:

It means: They said, "We acknowledge the oneness of Allah, and we affirm that there is no god besides Him." ﴿And we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him﴾: It means: We reject the deities that we used to associate in our worship of Allah before this time, and worship alongside Him, and take as gods; so we disown them.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿But their belief did not benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of Allah which has passed on among His servants. And the disbelievers were lost therein.﴾ (85)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Their affirmation in this world of the oneness of Allah did not benefit them at the moment of witnessing His punishment having descended and His chastisement having arrived, because they affirmed it at a time when affirmation benefits no one who affirms, since the judgment of Allah had already passed in His prior knowledge, that whoever repents after the descent of Allah's punishment for his disbelief, his repentance will not benefit him.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿But their belief did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾: When they saw the punishment of Allah in this world, their belief did not benefit them at that time.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿This is the way of Allah which has passed on among His servants﴾:

It means: Allah, blessed and exalted, withheld from them their reprieve, their acceptance of repentance from them, and their return to belief in Allah and affirmation of their messengers after witnessing His might which had descended upon them; this was His way which had passed among His creation, and therefore He did not reprieve them nor accept their repentance in that state.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿This is the way of Allah which has passed on among His servants﴾: He said, "Thus was the way of Allah with those who passed before, that when they witnessed the punishment of Allah, their belief did not benefit them at that time."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers were lost therein﴾:

It means: They perished at the arrival of the might of Allah, so their transaction was defrauded, and in their trade they exchanged the Hereafter for this world, and forgiveness for punishment, and belief for disbelief. The disbelievers are those who disbelieve in their Lord and deny the oneness of their Creator, taking others besides Him as gods to worship instead of their Originator.

End of the commentary on Surah Ha Mim al-Mu'min.
